rows.descriptionText:
About Eip

Energy Infrastructure Partners LLC (EIP) is a minority-owned business specializing in energy efficiency, electrification, decarbonization, and demand-side management programs. With offices in New York, Illinois, California, Oregon, Pennsylvania, and Washington, EIP combines national reach with local market understanding. Our work advances sustainable energy solutions, supports economic development, and prioritizes benefits for disadvantaged communities. As a leader in clean energy program implementation and consulting, EIP is proud to help clients achieve meaningful environmental and economic outcomes through innovative, high-impact projects.

Position Description

EIP is seeking a Model Analyst based in Chicago to conduct regression analysis and quantify energy savings for strategic energy management (SEM) programs serving ComEd, PECO, and NYSEG markets. The analyst will build and maintain facility-level energy use models that account for production, weather, occupancy, and other relevant drivers, then use those models to assess changes in performance over time.

Working with engineers, SEM coaches, program managers, and customer teams, the Model Analyst will gather and validate data, select appropriate model variables and time periods, establish baselines, calculate normalized savings, and prepare documentation that supports program reporting and technical review. The role requires careful statistical analysis and the judgment to distinguish meaningful operational improvements from data issues or changes in facility activity.

The ideal candidate can explain modeling assumptions and results clearly to technical and nontechnical colleagues, manage recurring analyses for multiple facilities, and adapt methods to each utility program’s measurement and verification requirements.

Objectives of this Role

Reliable Energy Baselines: Develop reproducible regression models that describe normal facility energy use and its relationship to relevant operating conditions. Defensible Savings Estimates: Quantify changes in energy use attributable to SEM activities using approved methods, documented adjustments, and appropriate uncertainty checks. Data Quality: Identify missing, inconsistent, or anomalous utility and driver data before they affect model results or savings claims. Program Compliance: Apply the applicable utility and program measurement and verification protocols consistently across participating facilities. Actionable Insight: Translate model findings into useful feedback for SEM coaches, engineers, customers, and program managers. Timely Delivery: Maintain models and recurring reports on schedule while supporting accurate portfolio-level tracking and continuous improvement. 

Daily and Monthly Responsibilities

Assemble Analysis Data: Collect and organize utility bills, interval meter data, production records, weather data, operating schedules, occupancy, and other drivers relevant to each facility. Validate Data Quality: Check units, time stamps, meter coverage, missing periods, duplicate records, outliers, and changes in operations; document corrections and unresolved limitations. Develop Regression Models: Select appropriate baseline periods and independent variables; build and test facility-level models using suitable statistical tools and program-approved methods. Evaluate Model Performance: Review residuals, explanatory power, bias, error metrics, and the plausibility of coefficients; investigate poor model fit and avoid unsupported savings conclusions. Calculate SEM Savings: Compare observed reporting-period energy use with modeled baseline consumption adjusted to reporting-period conditions; document formulas, inputs, and results. Address Facility Changes: Assess whether equipment, production, schedules, occupancy, or other non-routine changes require model revisions or documented adjustments under program rules. Support Measurement and Verification: Prepare model files, data dictionaries, calculation workbooks, charts, and narratives for internal review, utility reporting, and evaluator requests. Collaborate with Program Teams: Work with SEM coaches and engineers to understand facility operations, validate model drivers, investigate unexpected trends, and interpret results. Communicate Findings: Present baselines, performance trends, savings estimates, assumptions, and uncertainty in concise reports and visualizations suited to the intended audience. Maintain Portfolio Tracking: Update recurring analyses, track analysis status and due dates, reconcile facility results to program reporting, and escalate data or modeling risks. Improve Analytical Practices: Help refine templates, quality checks, documentation standards, and repeatable workflows across SEM programs. 

Required Qualifications

Education: Bachelor’s degree in engineering, statistics, mathematics, data science, economics, physics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent relevant experience. Regression Analysis: Demonstrated ability to develop, interpret, and validate multivariable regression models using real-world time-series or operational data. Data Analysis Tools: Strong Excel skills and proficiency with at least one analytical environment such as R, Python, SQL, or a comparable statistical tool. Analytical Judgment: Ability to assess model fit, data quality, variable selection, outliers, seasonality, and uncertainty without relying solely on automated outputs. Technical Documentation: Ability to maintain transparent calculations and explain methods, assumptions, adjustments, and results clearly in writing. Collaboration: Ability to work with engineers, customer-facing teams, and program managers to understand the operational context behind the data. Organization: Ability to manage analyses for multiple facilities and programs, maintain version control, and meet recurring reporting deadlines. 

Preferred Qualifications

SEM Experience: Experience developing energy baselines or calculating savings for strategic energy management, industrial energy management, or related utility programs. Measurement and Verification: Familiarity with whole-facility measurement and verification, normalized metered energy consumption approaches, IPMVP Option C, or utility-specific SEM protocols. Energy Data: Experience working with utility interval data, billing data, weather normalization, industrial production data, or building management system trends. Statistical Methods: Experience evaluating model bias, normalized mean bias error, coefficient of variation of root mean squared error, confidence intervals, or comparable model quality measures where appropriate. Energy Systems: Familiarity with commercial or industrial energy systems and common factors that influence facility energy consumption. Program Markets: Experience supporting ComEd, PECO, NYSEG, or other utility energy efficiency programs. 

WE OFFER

Competitive base salary commensurate with experience and qualifications. ($60k-$75k)Performance-based bonus tied to individual and company performance. 401(k) retirement savings plan with employer match. Comprehensive health, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance. Paid vacation, sick time, and holidays. Professional development and training opportunities. A dynamic, inclusive work environment that encourages collaboration, innovation, and growth. 

Join us!

At EIP, your analysis will help organizations see whether changes in how they operate are producing measurable energy savings. You will bring statistical rigor and practical judgment to SEM programs across multiple utility markets.

Energy Infrastructure Partners is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Note: This is a Chicago-based hybrid position. EIP generally requires four days per week in office when not traveling. Specific in-office requirements will be based on program needs.

EIP does not offer visa sponsorship for this position.

Your responsibilities will include onboarding and guiding client users on YouGov’s products, leveraging those systems to build reports and conduct ad hoc analyses, and delivering analytical insights and recommendations to our customers. You will support YouGov clients ranging from Fortune 100s to fast-growing companies, spanning a variety of industries including Retail, FMCG, Food & Dining, Financial Services, Insurance, Technology, Social Media, Advertising Agencies, and more.

Job Responsibilities

Responsibilities

In this role you will be working closely with senior members of the Client Service team to ensure we are driving successful outcomes for our clients. You will gain valuable experience and develop a broad skill set through your on the job responsibilities, specifically:

Data Product Fluency: Become knowledgeable in all of YouGov’s tools, gaining a deep understanding of the user interfaces and data, translating that knowledge to our clientsTeaching Others: Support onboarding and ongoing training efforts with new and existing clients to ensure they are getting the most value out of our data productsAnalytic Application: Design and deliver re-occurring Insights reports to clients addressing their core insight needs, including (but not limited to) Brand Tracking, Market Sizing, and Audience Identification & ProfilingInsights Discovery & Story Telling: Deliver data-driven insights and recommendations, addressing client’s ad hoc business questionsInternal Collaboration: Partnering with commercial and product dev teams to provide a positive client experience that promotes partnership growth

Qualifications, Skills & Experience

This is an entry-level role, with qualifications focusing more on competencies than prior experiences. The applicant should be interested in the market research industry and working directly with clients.

Intellectually curious, with a strong interest in solving problems with data and story tellingEnthusiastic, a willing and quick learner with a drive to succeedService-oriented mentality, with a desire to work in a client facing roleStrong communication skills and ability to craft a persuasive narrativeUncompromising attention to detailAbility to manage multiple projects simultaneouslyEffective team player, eager to collaborate with teammates and clients

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree or higher. A degree in a marketing or a research field is a plus (i.e., economics, psychology, business, marketing, market research, analytics, etc.)Strong knowledge of Microsoft Office’s Word, Excel, and PowerPointAn eye for detail and ability to put together accurate deliverables in a timely fashion

Nice To Haves

Prior work experience as a researcher or analyst, or experience of converting data into storiesExperience of working on client-facing projectsKnowledge of business intelligence programs (ex. Tableau, PowerBI, etc.)Experience leveraging AI for data visualization and storytelling

Join our global team to help us achieve our social mission: to make millions of people’s opinions heard for the benefit of our local, national, and international communities.

Job Description

Our quantitative strategists are at the cutting edge of our business and solve real-world problems through a variety of analytical methods. As a member of our team, you will utilize your training in mathematics, programming, and logical thinking to build quantitative models that drive success in our business. Your problem-solving talents and aptitude for innovation will help define your contributions and enable you to find solutions to a broad range of problems, in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.

Responsibilities

As a strategist on our PWM Risk Strats team, you will work closely with various teams including risk management and fraud strategy. You will combine quantitative techniques and industry knowledge to build best in class models and tools that streamline risk management, detect fraud at scale, enable optimized data-driven business decision making, and optimize profitability.

Responsibilities Include

 Developing and deploying ML models for fraud and anomaly detection as well as business workflows enhancement  Delivering risk metrics and quantitative analytics for financial and non-financial risks across wealth management  Develop AI-led solutions to improve efficiency and accuracy in risk management.  Building and maintaining robust and systematic risk management tools and reporting  Collaborating on the design of new and existing strategies to address clients’ investment goals.  Developing and maintaining risk management and portfolio analysis tools across multiple asset classes for senior management and portfolio managers.  Building and maintaining infrastructure of Strategists’ analytical systems. 

About Goldman Sachs Wealth Management

Across Wealth Management, Goldman Sachs helps empower clients and customers around the world to reach their financial goals. Our consumer business provides digital solutions for customers to better spend, borrow, invest, and save. Across Wealth Management, our growth is driven by a relentless focus on our people, our clients and customers, and leading-edge technology, data, and design.

 Bachelor, Masters or Ph.D. in a quantitative or engineering field, e.g. mathematics, physics, quantitative finance, computational finance, computer science, engineering  1-3 years of experience in the job offered or related quantitative financial modeling and software development positions  Programming and mathematical skills are required  Creativity, problem-solving skills, and ability to communicate complex ideas to a variety of audiences  A self-starter, should have ability to work independently as well as thrive in a team environment  Excellent understanding of machine learning techniques and algorithms, such as gradient boosting decision trees, random forests, etc., is a plus  Experience with building models using common data science toolkits, i.e., Python (Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn) and Spark  Experience with prompt engineering, working with LLM models, and MCP.  Previous work experience in: Utilizing statistical methods, including time-series and regression analysis; programming in object-oriented languages for efficient model implementations; manipulating data sets using relational databases and SQL

Previous work experience in: Utilizing statistical methods, including time-series and regression analysis; programming in object-oriented languages for efficient model implementations; manipulating data sets using relational databases and SQL

job purpose:

The Operations Data Analyst will play a critical role in advancing fairlife's data driven manufacturing operations to drive continuous improvement on key performance indicators. This position is responsible for collaborating with the Operations Teams and the Decision Intelligence (DI) teams to develop data analytics solutions to enable decision making in support of Operational Excellence. This role will leverage fairlife's Unified Factory Data Model (UFDM) and analytics platform to create reporting and analytic solutions to enable operational decision making at each of the factories

Collaborate with factory leadership and cross-functional teams to understand requirements and implement data and reporting strategies aligned with operational goals.Lead the development, deployment, and maintenance of Power BI dashboards and reports that support decision-making at all levels of the factory.Analyze operational datasets to uncover insights and trends to enable decision making at all levels of the organization.Drive the adoption and integration of the UFDM and analytics platform at each of the manufacturing facilities and throughout Operations.Partner with engineering, IT, and DI teams to identify and acquire new machine-level data points and ensure data accuracy and completeness through validation.Maintain consistent visual and reporting standards across multiple Power BI workspaces and applications.Ensure data governance practices are aligned and upheld within the Decision Intelligence teams strategic framework.Provide training and support to end users to enhance data literacy and ensure effective use of BI tools.

skills/qualifications required: 

 Bachelor's degree in Analytics, Data Science, Computer Science, or a related field; or equivalent professional experience. Strong technical expertise in data modeling, visualization, and analytics, as well as the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional stakeholders. Proficiency in SQL and DAX programming languages. Demonstrated experience in developing and managing Power BI dashboards and reports. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a strong attention to detail and data accuracy. Excellent communication and documentation skills, with the ability to translate business needs into technical solutions. Detail oriented to ensure data integrity and accuracy Self-starter with a growth mindset and a passion for data Ability to handle ambiguity and work in a fast paced, entrepreneurial environment

requirement- 40 hours per week with additional hours as required.Ability to flex shift as needed. Possible 3 hours sitting/3 hours standing/2 hours walking.Ability to lift up to 50 lbs.  Strong practical understanding of quantitative finance models, including stochastic calculus and their application to real-world investment and risk management challenges. EIP is seeking a Model Analyst based in Chicago to conduct regression analysis and quantify energy savings for strategic energy management (SEM) programs serving ComEd, PECO, and NYSEG markets. The analyst will build and maintain facility-level energy use models that account for production, weather, occupancy, and other relevant drivers, then use those models to assess changes in performance over time.

Working with engineers, SEM coaches, program managers, and customer teams, the Model Analyst will gather and validate data, select appropriate model variables and time periods, establish baselines, calculate normalized savings, and prepare documentation that supports program reporting and technical review. The role requires careful statistical analysis and the judgment to distinguish meaningful operational improvements from data issues or changes in facility activity.

The ideal candidate can explain modeling assumptions and results clearly to technical and nontechnical colleagues, manage recurring analyses for multiple facilities, and adapt methods to each utility program’s measurement and verification requirements.

Objectives of this Role

Reliable Energy Baselines: Develop reproducible regression models that describe normal facility energy use and its relationship to relevant operating conditions. Defensible Savings Estimates: Quantify changes in energy use attributable to SEM activities using approved methods, documented adjustments, and appropriate uncertainty checks. Data Quality: Identify missing, inconsistent, or anomalous utility and driver data before they affect model results or savings claims. Program Compliance: Apply the applicable utility and program measurement and verification protocols consistently across participating facilities. Actionable Insight: Translate model findings into useful feedback for SEM coaches, engineers, customers, and program managers. Timely Delivery: Maintain models and recurring reports on schedule while supporting accurate portfolio-level tracking and continuous improvement. 

Daily and Monthly Responsibilities

Assemble Analysis Data: Collect and organize utility bills, interval meter data, production records, weather data, operating schedules, occupancy, and other drivers relevant to each facility. Validate Data Quality: Check units, time stamps, meter coverage, missing periods, duplicate records, outliers, and changes in operations; document corrections and unresolved limitations. Develop Regression Models: Select appropriate baseline periods and independent variables; build and test facility-level models using suitable statistical tools and program-approved methods. Evaluate Model Performance: Review residuals, explanatory power, bias, error metrics, and the plausibility of coefficients; investigate poor model fit and avoid unsupported savings conclusions. Calculate SEM Savings: Compare observed reporting-period energy use with modeled baseline consumption adjusted to reporting-period conditions; document formulas, inputs, and results. Address Facility Changes: Assess whether equipment, production, schedules, occupancy, or other non-routine changes require model revisions or documented adjustments under program rules. Support Measurement and Verification: Prepare model files, data dictionaries, calculation workbooks, charts, and narratives for internal review, utility reporting, and evaluator requests. Collaborate with Program Teams: Work with SEM coaches and engineers to understand facility operations, validate model drivers, investigate unexpected trends, and interpret results. Communicate Findings: Present baselines, performance trends, savings estimates, assumptions, and uncertainty in concise reports and visualizations suited to the intended audience. Maintain Portfolio Tracking: Update recurring analyses, track analysis status and due dates, reconcile facility results to program reporting, and escalate data or modeling risks. Improve Analytical Practices: Help refine templates, quality checks, documentation standards, and repeatable workflows across SEM programs. 

Required Qualifications

Education: Bachelor’s degree in engineering, statistics, mathematics, data science, economics, physics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent relevant experience. Regression Analysis: Demonstrated ability to develop, interpret, and validate multivariable regression models using real-world time-series or operational data. Data Analysis Tools: Strong Excel skills and proficiency with at least one analytical environment such as R, Python, SQL, or a comparable statistical tool. Analytical Judgment: Ability to assess model fit, data quality, variable selection, outliers, seasonality, and uncertainty without relying solely on automated outputs. Technical Documentation: Ability to maintain transparent calculations and explain methods, assumptions, adjustments, and results clearly in writing. Collaboration: Ability to work with engineers, customer-facing teams, and program managers to understand the operational context behind the data. Organization: Ability to manage analyses for multiple facilities and programs, maintain version control, and meet recurring reporting deadlines. 

Preferred Qualifications

SEM Experience: Experience developing energy baselines or calculating savings for strategic energy management, industrial energy management, or related utility programs. Measurement and Verification: Familiarity with whole-facility measurement and verification, normalized metered energy consumption approaches, IPMVP Option C, or utility-specific SEM protocols. Energy Data: Experience working with utility interval data, billing data, weather normalization, industrial production data, or building management system trends. Statistical Methods: Experience evaluating model bias, normalized mean bias error, coefficient of variation of root mean squared error, confidence intervals, or comparable model quality measures where appropriate. Energy Systems: Familiarity with commercial or industrial energy systems and common factors that influence facility energy consumption. Program Markets: Experience supporting ComEd, PECO, NYSEG, or other utility energy efficiency programs. 

WE OFFER

Competitive base salary commensurate with experience and qualifications. ($60k-$75k)Performance-based bonus tied to individual and company performance. 401(k) retirement savings plan with employer match. Comprehensive health, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance. Paid vacation, sick time, and holidays. Professional development and training opportunities. A dynamic, inclusive work environment that encourages collaboration, innovation, and growth. 

Join us!

At EIP, your analysis will help organizations see whether changes in how they operate are producing measurable energy savings. You will bring statistical rigor and practical judgment to SEM programs across multiple utility markets.

Energy Infrastructure Partners is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Note: This is a Chicago-based hybrid position. EIP generally requires four days per week in office when not traveling. Specific in-office requirements will be based on program needs.

EIP does not offer visa sponsorship for this position.

rows.title: Psychiatric Social Health Tech
rows.descriptionText:
Marketing Statement

Lincoln Medical and Mental Health Center is one of New York City’s premier acute care hospitals. Located in Downtown Bronx, Lincoln is a teaching hospital renowned for its Centers of Excellence, and a recognized industry leader in the implementation of state-of-the art medical technology and best practices. Our team of highly trained and caring medical professionals is dedicated to providing the highest quality health care that is safe, compassionate, culturally competent and patient-centered. Comprehensive services are offered in three major primary care areas: Medicine, Pediatrics, and Women’s Health in addition to more than eighty (80) specialty services. At Lincoln, the safety and comfort of our patients is our number one priority.

At NYC Health + Hospitals, our mission is to deliver high quality care health services, without exception. Every employee takes a person-centered approach that exemplifies the ICARE values (Integrity, Compassion, Accountability, Respect, and Excellence) through empathic communication and partnerships between all persons.

Duties & Responsibilities

Purpose of Position:

Under the direct supervision of a professional Nurse or other assigned professional staff member, performs functions related to assisting patients with activities of daily living and personal hygiene, and participates as a member of a treatment, nursing or health care team in implementing appropriate regimens for patients who are in Behavioral Health service areas. Acts in compliance with health care system and all relevant regulatory policies.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

 Observes patient’s physical condition, mental state and social behavior and reports to team leader or Nurse-in-charge and provides individual nursing care for patients who are acutely ill, either physically or emotionally. Participates in planning and implementing an orientation program for new patients. Gathers information for intake, social histories, referrals and related purposes which would augment the understanding of cases. Participates in planning and implementing daily living activities on the ward for patients and contributes to the development of a therapeutic ward environment. Assists in planning and implementing therapeutic activities with groups of hospitalized psychiatric patients and encourages client involvement in various individual and group activities as part of planned treatment programs. Assists with the physical care and personal hygiene of selected patients, consisting of, but not limited to: bathing, turning and positioning, skin care, passive and active range of motion, mouth care, foot care, nail care, applying hot and cold packs, etc. Assists patients with meal selection and feeds patients if necessary, delivers/removes trays, distributes water, nourishment, ice, etc. With successful completion of NYC Health + Hospitals program, assists behavioral health team in the application and removal of restraints and the implementation of restraints/seclusion, when deemed necessary by appropriate personnel, ensuring the physical and emotional health and safety of the patient when using such methods. On the direction of a registered nurse or other professional staff member, either individually or as part of behavioral health team may escort patient to required location(s), within and outside of the health care setting. Takes patient vital signs, when directed to do so by clinical staff, and enters patient vital sign data into the electronic medical record performs finger stick tests. Changes linen and makes beds. Keeps ward and/or unit, linen, utility, treatment, storage rooms and recreational areas in a neat and orderly fashion. Disinfects personal items with appropriate disinfectant products, when required. May perform functions and activities of the basic Nurse’s Aide in support of the above tasks, and other related work, as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

 High school diploma or its educational equivalent, approved by a State’s Department of Education or a

recognized accrediting organization; and

 *Successful completion of NYC Health + Hospitals training program in the application and use of restraints and

seclusion must be completed prior to an individual performing such work; and

 Successful completion of NYC Health + Hospitals training in the performance of vital signs and grooming within

ninety (90) calendar days of appointment to the title; and

 Holds or obtains a valid and current certification in Basic Life Support (BLS) through the American Heart Association

(AHA) within sixty (60) calendar days of appointment to the title.

Department Preferences

How To Apply

If you wish to apply for this position, please apply online by clicking the "Apply for Job" button.

rows.title: Social Content Creator

rows.descriptionText:
Blossom Health exists to solve the mental health epidemic in America by partnering with psychiatrists to expand access to affordable, timely, clinically-effective mental healthcare. Our AI-native care platform is loved by hundreds of clinicians and tens of thousands of patients.

We’re a Series A company with $20M+ raised from Headline, Village Global, and the founders of General Catalyst, Flatiron Health, Sword Health, Fay, Elemy, Zip, Blank Street, Assured, Bridge, Birches Health, and Enzo Health.

The Role:

We’re looking for a Founding Social & Content Creator to build Blossom’s social presence into a major engine for brand awareness, trust, and growth.

This is not a traditional social media manager role. We’re looking for someone who can take an idea from a blank page to something people actually want to watch, share, save, and talk about.

You’ll own Blossom’s organic presence across TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook from end to end: developing concepts, filming, editing, publishing, engaging with our community, studying performance, and figuring out what to make next.

You’ll also create UGC-style content that can cross over into paid acquisition, working closely with our marketing team to develop hooks, concepts, and creative variations for Meta and TikTok.

This is a highly autonomous role. We want someone who has strong creative instincts, moves quickly, understands internet culture, and is excited to build our platforms rather than inherit an existing playbook.

Why You Should Work Here:

🚀 Build something from the ground up: You’ll have the opportunity to shape how one of the fastest-growing mental healthcare companies in the country shows up online🎥 Actually create: This isn't a role where you brief agencies all day. You'll have the autonomy to ideate, shoot, edit, publish, experiment, and iterate yourself📈 Your work will be measurable: We want to build social into a real growth channel, not just a place where we post company updates🧠 Make mental healthcare interesting: Turn complicated, sensitive, and sometimes intimidating topics into content people actually want to consume and share⚡ Move fast: Test ideas quickly, learn what works, double down on winners, and kill what doesn't🤝 High trust and autonomy: We care about results and creative judgment. You'll have significant ownership over what Blossom looks and sounds like online

What You'll Do:

Own Blossom’s day-to-day presence across TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, and emerging social platformsDevelop Blossom’s organic social strategy, recurring content formats, creative concepts, and publishing cadenceConcept, script, film, edit, and publish short-form video from start to finishBe comfortable appearing on camera and pulling other members of the Blossom team into contentBuild repeatable content franchises that audiences recognize and want to come back toIdentify trends, conversations, hooks, and formats early and figure out how Blossom can participate without sounding forced or corporateCreate UGC-style paid creative for Meta and TikTok, including multiple hooks, cuts, and calls to action for testingWork with creators, clinicians, patients, and members of our team to source and produce compelling contentManage and grow our social community through comments, DMs, and conversationsNavigate mental-health content thoughtfully while following privacy, clinical review, and escalation guidelinesTrack performance across views, reach, watch time, shares, saves, follower growth, profile visits, and site trafficUse performance data to constantly refine what we create and where we invest our timeStay obsessed with what is happening on the internet and continuously experiment with new formats, platforms, creators, and ideas

You'll Be a Good Fit If:

You have 1–3 years of experience creating content or running social for a brand, startup, agency, creator, or your own audienceYou have personally grown a social account to 50K+ followers or can show comparable evidence of meaningful audience growthYou’ve created content that has generated 1M+ organic views within a 90-day periodYou have a portfolio of short-form content that you personally concepted, filmed, and editedYou understand why certain videos take off and can break down the hook, pacing, format, audience, and distribution behind themYou’re fluent in TikTok, Instagram Reels, Stories, Facebook, and short-form internet cultureYou can edit quickly in CapCut, Premiere, or similar toolsYou understand what makes organic content different from paid creative and can make content that works in both environmentsYou’re comfortable on camera and comfortable directing other people on cameraYou’re highly self-directed. You don't need someone handing you a content calendar every MondayYou have strong creative judgment and aren't afraid to test weird ideasYou move quickly and would rather publish, learn, and iterate than spend two weeks debating a single postYou have good judgment around sensitive topics and understand that mental healthcare requires a higher bar for accuracy and trustYou’re authorized to work in the United StatesYou’re excited to be in-person in New York City 5 days a week

Bonus: You’ve built an audience from zero, created paid social ads that converted, worked with creators or influencers, or created content in healthcare, wellness, consumer, or another regulated category.

What We're Looking For:

Internet native - you understand what people are watching, sharing, talking about, and whyCreator first - you don't just manage content; you make itHighly self-directed - you can turn a broad goal into ideas, content, experiments, and results without waiting for instructionsCreative and analytical - you care equally about making something great and understanding whether it workedHigh velocity - you can produce a lot, learn quickly, and keep raising the barStrong taste - you know when something feels fresh, interesting, funny, useful, or painfully corporateComfortable experimenting - you're willing to try ten ideas to find the one that takes offOwnership mindset - you think about Blossom's audience and platforms like they're your ownHumble - you care more about making great work and growing the brand than getting credit for every idea

What Success Looks Like:

We want someone who is excited by an ambitious goal: turn Blossom into a mental-health brand people actually want to follow.

In your first few months, that means rapidly testing formats, establishing Blossom's voice, finding repeatable content winners, and building meaningful organic momentum.

We aren't hiring someone to simply keep our feeds active. We're hiring someone who wants to prove they can build an audience from the ground up.

Compensation & Benefits:

$70,000–$85,000 base salary, based on experienceMeaningful equity ownershipSignificant growth opportunities as Blossom and the marketing team scaleBeautiful, sunshine and snack-filled office in the heart of Flatiron, ManhattanHealth, dental, and vision insuranceA focus on outcomes, not hoursTeam outings and offsitesUnlimited PTO

Compensation Range: $70K - $85K

VettaFi was created by unifying complementary businesses who shared a vision for client success, the value of relationships, and the importance of data. Brands such as ETF Trends, ETF Database, Alerian, and S-Network Global Indexes merged to form VettaFi in 2022. Your work will directly support VettaFi’s diverse client base, helping them launch and manage innovative financial products, both exchange-traded and non-exchange-traded.

Relevant Experience: Proven experience in financial indexing, structured products, portfolio analysis, or research. Analytical Skills: Ability to identify issues, analyze data, synthesize information, and provide actionable recommendations. Organizational Skills: Excellent time management, prioritization, and ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and deadlines. Comfort and confidence in speaking to groups, including both internal teams and external stakeholders or clients, including those unfamiliar with the subject matter. rows.title: Model Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
About Eip

Energy Infrastructure Partners LLC (EIP) is a minority-owned business specializing in energy efficiency, electrification, decarbonization, and demand-side management programs. With offices in New York, Illinois, California, Oregon, Pennsylvania, and Washington, EIP combines national reach with local market understanding. Our work advances sustainable energy solutions, supports economic development, and prioritizes benefits for disadvantaged communities. As a leader in clean energy program implementation and consulting, EIP is proud to help clients achieve meaningful environmental and economic outcomes through innovative, high-impact projects.

Position Description

EIP is seeking a Model Analyst based in Chicago to conduct regression analysis and quantify energy savings for strategic energy management (SEM) programs serving ComEd, PECO, and NYSEG markets. The analyst will build and maintain facility-level energy use models that account for production, weather, occupancy, and other relevant drivers, then use those models to assess changes in performance over time.

Working with engineers, SEM coaches, program managers, and customer teams, the Model Analyst will gather and validate data, select appropriate model variables and time periods, establish baselines, calculate normalized savings, and prepare documentation that supports program reporting and technical review. The role requires careful statistical analysis and the judgment to distinguish meaningful operational improvements from data issues or changes in facility activity.

The ideal candidate can explain modeling assumptions and results clearly to technical and nontechnical colleagues, manage recurring analyses for multiple facilities, and adapt methods to each utility program’s measurement and verification requirements.

Objectives of this Role

Reliable Energy Baselines: Develop reproducible regression models that describe normal facility energy use and its relationship to relevant operating conditions. Defensible Savings Estimates: Quantify changes in energy use attributable to SEM activities using approved methods, documented adjustments, and appropriate uncertainty checks. Data Quality: Identify missing, inconsistent, or anomalous utility and driver data before they affect model results or savings claims. Program Compliance: Apply the applicable utility and program measurement and verification protocols consistently across participating facilities. Actionable Insight: Translate model findings into useful feedback for SEM coaches, engineers, customers, and program managers. Timely Delivery: Maintain models and recurring reports on schedule while supporting accurate portfolio-level tracking and continuous improvement. 

Daily and Monthly Responsibilities

Assemble Analysis Data: Collect and organize utility bills, interval meter data, production records, weather data, operating schedules, occupancy, and other drivers relevant to each facility. Validate Data Quality: Check units, time stamps, meter coverage, missing periods, duplicate records, outliers, and changes in operations; document corrections and unresolved limitations. Develop Regression Models: Select appropriate baseline periods and independent variables; build and test facility-level models using suitable statistical tools and program-approved methods. Evaluate Model Performance: Review residuals, explanatory power, bias, error metrics, and the plausibility of coefficients; investigate poor model fit and avoid unsupported savings conclusions. Calculate SEM Savings: Compare observed reporting-period energy use with modeled baseline consumption adjusted to reporting-period conditions; document formulas, inputs, and results. Address Facility Changes: Assess whether equipment, production, schedules, occupancy, or other non-routine changes require model revisions or documented adjustments under program rules. Support Measurement and Verification: Prepare model files, data dictionaries, calculation workbooks, charts, and narratives for internal review, utility reporting, and evaluator requests. Collaborate with Program Teams: Work with SEM coaches and engineers to understand facility operations, validate model drivers, investigate unexpected trends, and interpret results. Communicate Findings: Present baselines, performance trends, savings estimates, assumptions, and uncertainty in concise reports and visualizations suited to the intended audience. Maintain Portfolio Tracking: Update recurring analyses, track analysis status and due dates, reconcile facility results to program reporting, and escalate data or modeling risks. Improve Analytical Practices: Help refine templates, quality checks, documentation standards, and repeatable workflows across SEM programs. 

Required Qualifications

Education: Bachelor’s degree in engineering, statistics, mathematics, data science, economics, physics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent relevant experience. Regression Analysis: Demonstrated ability to develop, interpret, and validate multivariable regression models using real-world time-series or operational data. Data Analysis Tools: Strong Excel skills and proficiency with at least one analytical environment such as R, Python, SQL, or a comparable statistical tool. Analytical Judgment: Ability to assess model fit, data quality, variable selection, outliers, seasonality, and uncertainty without relying solely on automated outputs. Technical Documentation: Ability to maintain transparent calculations and explain methods, assumptions, adjustments, and results clearly in writing. Collaboration: Ability to work with engineers, customer-facing teams, and program managers to understand the operational context behind the data. Organization: Ability to manage analyses for multiple facilities and programs, maintain version control, and meet recurring reporting deadlines. 

Preferred Qualifications

SEM Experience: Experience developing energy baselines or calculating savings for strategic energy management, industrial energy management, or related utility programs. Measurement and Verification: Familiarity with whole-facility measurement and verification, normalized metered energy consumption approaches, IPMVP Option C, or utility-specific SEM protocols. Energy Data: Experience working with utility interval data, billing data, weather normalization, industrial production data, or building management system trends. Statistical Methods: Experience evaluating model bias, normalized mean bias error, coefficient of variation of root mean squared error, confidence intervals, or comparable model quality measures where appropriate. Energy Systems: Familiarity with commercial or industrial energy systems and common factors that influence facility energy consumption. Program Markets: Experience supporting ComEd, PECO, NYSEG, or other utility energy efficiency programs. 

WE OFFER

Competitive base salary commensurate with experience and qualifications. ($60k-$75k)Performance-based bonus tied to individual and company performance. 401(k) retirement savings plan with employer match. Comprehensive health, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance. Paid vacation, sick time, and holidays. Professional development and training opportunities. A dynamic, inclusive work environment that encourages collaboration, innovation, and growth. 

Join us!

At EIP, your analysis will help organizations see whether changes in how they operate are producing measurable energy savings. You will bring statistical rigor and practical judgment to SEM programs across multiple utility markets.

Energy Infrastructure Partners is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Note: This is a Chicago-based hybrid position. EIP generally requires four days per week in office when not traveling. Specific in-office requirements will be based on program needs.

EIP does not offer visa sponsorship for this position.

Job Summary Lab of Dr. Prashant Rajbhandari in the Diabetes, Obesity, and Metabolism Institute (DOMI) has an opening for an entry level Associate Researcher I. Rajbhandari Lab is broadly interested in 1) Immune cell regulation of lipid metabolism (Cell 2018; Cell Metabolism 2020), 2) developmental process of brown/beige and white fat (Cell Reports 2023; Nature Communication 2024), and 3) mammary gland adipose biology (Nature 2023), and 4) crosstalk between adipose and other metabolic tissues (esp liver) in the setting of obesity. To address these topics, the lab uses cell and molecular biology, biochemistry, Next-gen sequencing (ChIP-, RNA-, ATAC-seq), animal model, single cell/nuclei RNA sequencing, and imaging. The broader significance of the work in Rajbhandari Lab is that obesity is linked to various diseases and by studying how cellular and molecular pathways are perturbed in the setting of obesity might provide better understanding of this disease.

About Us

BBC Studios’ Direct-to-Consumer (DTC) business brings premium content directly to North American audiences through two distinctive streaming brands: BritBox and BBC Select.

BritBox, the ultimate streaming destination for British TV. We offer an unparalleled collection of thoughtfully curated entertainment—cleverly crafted and full of the charm, wit, and heart that define British storytelling.

If you’re passionate about entertainment, thrive in a fast-paced environment, and want to play a meaningful role in our growth journey, this is your opportunity to be part of a dynamic Direct-to-Consumer business within BBC Studios, bringing the very best of British TV to fans everywhere.

Job Purpose

As Experimentation Analyst, you will collaborate closely with multiple departments such as Marketing, Creative, UX and Product to design, execute, and monitor tests. Through testing, you’ll deliver improved results in areas such as paid media, key subscription metrics including trial-to-paid conversion, LTV and retention, and help ensure new launches and tactics are successful from the get-go.

Alongside this, you will help manage the day-to-day A/B testing workflow, from test intake through to results summaries and sharing learnings across the business. You will also communicate regularly with stakeholders to ensure tests are aligned, progress is visible, and insights are translated into clear actions.

This is an opportunity for a self-starter who can dig in and use both data-driven insights and testing techniques to drive growth within our company.

Responsibilities

Test Setup & Execution: Assist in designing and implementing A/B tests and multivariate tests for marketing campaigns, creative assets, and subscriber strategies in product/app, email, push etc.Project Management: Ensure all tests are tracked centrally, making all relevant updates to details and dates, proactively identifying conflicts and ensuring tests will start and end on agreed timelines.Monitoring & Reporting: Regularly monitor test performance, analyze results, and compile reports that detail findings and recommendations for future campaigns.Data Analysis: Utilize analytics tools to evaluate user behavior and conversion metrics, identifying trends and actionable insights to enhance marketing efforts.Collaboration: Work closely with the Senior Manager, marketing team, and creative team to ensure tests align with business goals and user needs.Subscriber Strategy Support: Contribute to the development of strategies aimed at attracting new subscribers and improving retention through data-driven insights.Continuous Improvement: Stay informed about industry trends and best practices in testing and optimization, integrating new methodologies to improve testing processes.Documentation & Communication: Maintain clear documentation of testing protocols and communicate results effectively to stakeholders, ensuring alignment on strategic decisions.

Qualifications

rows.title: Manager, Data Scientist, Travel Intelligence, Hotels

parsed.text: New York City, NY, United States

rows.descriptionText:
Data is at the center of everything we do. As a startup, we disrupted the credit card industry by individually personalizing every credit card offer using statistical modeling and the relational database, cutting edge technology in 1988! Fast-forward a few years, and this little innovation and our passion for data has skyrocketed us to a Fortune 200 company and a leader in the world of data-driven decision-making.

As a Data Scientist at Capital One, you’ll be part of a team that’s leading the next wave of disruption at a whole new scale, using the latest in computing and machine learning technologies and operating across billions of customer records to unlock the big opportunities that help everyday people save money, time and agony in their financial lives.

Team Description

You will be a member of the Travel Intelligence team, a high-impact group dedicated to building the "intelligent core" of Capital One Travel. Our mission is to transform vast amounts of travel data into personalized, seamless experiences for our customers. Specifically, this role focuses on the Hotels domain, where you will own the end-to-end technical strategy for Search & Sort and Pricing Optimization. We operate in a "green-field" environment, moving from offline, historical data models to sophisticated, real-time Machine Learning solutions. As part of Travel Intelligence, you won't just be building models; you'll be partnering closely with Product and Engineering to define key metrics (like MOB and Reference Price coverage) and architecting the systems that determine what our customers see and what they pay. This is a unique opportunity to apply the 80:20 rule—starting with pragmatic, high-impact wins while simultaneously building the business case and technical roadmap for the future of ML at Capital One Travel.

Role Description

In this role, you will:

Partner with a cross-functional team of data scientists, software engineers, and product managers to deliver a product customers loveLeverage a broad stack of technologies — Python, Conda, AWS, H2O, Spark, and more — to reveal the insights hidden within huge volumes of numeric and textual dataBuild machine learning models through all phases of development, from design through training, evaluation, validation, and implementationFlex your interpersonal skills to translate the complexity of your work into tangible business goals

The Ideal Candidate is:

Customer first. You love the process of analyzing and creating, but also share our passion to do the right thing. You know at the end of the day it’s about making the right decision for our customers. Creative. You thrive on bringing definition to big, undefined problems. You love asking questions and pushing hard to find answers. You’re not afraid to share a new idea. Technical. You’re comfortable with open-source languages and are passionate about developing further. You have hands-on experience developing data science solutions using open-source tools and cloud computing platforms. A data guru. “Big data” doesn’t faze you. You have the skills to retrieve, combine, and analyze data from a variety of sources and structures. You know understanding the data is often the key to great data science. 

Basic Qualifications:

Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining one of the following with an expectation that the required degree will be obtained on or before the scheduled start date:A Bachelor's Degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) plus 6 years of experience performing data analyticsA Master's Degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) or an MBA with a quantitative concentration plus 4 years of experience performing data analyticsA PhD in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) plus 1 year of experience performing data analyticsAt least 1 year of experience leveraging open source programming languages for large scale data analysisAt least 1 year of experience working with machine learningAt least 1 year of experience utilizing relational databases

Preferred Qualifications:

PhD in “STEM” field (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics) plus 4 years of experience in data analyticsAt least 1 year of experience working with AWSAt least 5 years’ experience in Python, Scala, or R for large scale data analysisAt least 5 years’ experience with machine learning

Capital One will consider sponsoring a new qualified applicant for employment authorization for this position.

rows.title: Internship, Data Analysis and Report Synthesis with UNDP RBAS in NY, USA (Office-Based)

parsed.text: New York City, NY, United States

rows.descriptionText:
Job Description

Background

Anchored in the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and in line with the priorities outlined in the UNDP Strategic Plan, the Regional Bureau for Arab States (RBAS) supports the Arab States region to achieve sustainable development by eradicating poverty in all its forms and dimensions, accelerating structural transformations for sustainable development, and building resilience to crises and shocks. Within this work, the Regional Bureau for Arab States responds to needs across development settings including Least Developed Countries, Middle Income Countries, Net Contributor Countries and countries affected by crisis, with a view to support the building of resilience, fight climate change, leverage the promise of innovation, and prioritize the advance of women, youth and vulnerable groups as part of its commitment to the principles of universality, equality and leaving no one behind in an increasing challenging regional context which has been further impacted by various crises.

RBAS supports partners in the region to develop integrated, transformative, and scalable solutions to tackle the interconnected challenges of poverty, vulnerability, inequality and exclusion, in ways that are economically, socially and environmentally sustainable. The team assists in enhancing prospects for inclusive growth, jobs and livelihoods at national and local levels, including through economic recovery and resilience-building in crisis and post crisis contexts, focusing on empowering women and youth, and advancing opportunities for the most vulnerable. It also supports research, policy, and program guidance around: macroeconomic stability, private and financial sectors, fiscal policy and public finance management, economic transformation, social protection, women economic empowerment, urban and digital economy, etc.

The intern will report to the Strategic Initiatives Advisor in RBAS New York and will support the work on policy and research, including the Arab Human Development Report (AHDR) and ongoing socio-economic analyses examining the implications of conflicts and other shocks for growth, employment, poverty, inequality and human development in the Arab States region.

Duties And Responsibilities

Research and analysis: Conducting data collection, desk reviews of existing research and literature on one or two of the areas that the inclusive growth team is currently working on (namely, macroeconomics, public finance management, social protection, informality, labor market, poverty and inequality, private sector development (including micro, small and medium enterprises), SDG financing).Policy Brief Development: Assist in the drafting and preparation of policy briefs, technical notes, and economic assessments tailored for regional stakeholders and decision-makers.Advanced Quantitative Analysis: Support the team by conducting quantitative data analysis using reliable sources and tools to identify and visualize regional economic trends.Event and Dialogue Support: Provide logistical and substantive support in organizing regional consultations, webinars, and other forums related to inclusive growth and economic development.Regional Monitoring: Regularly monitor and summarize macroeconomic indicators, ongoing socio-economic developments, and policy shifts across the Arab States region to inform the team's ongoing programmatic work.Knowledge Management: Assist in maintaining and updating internal databases, knowledge repositories, and community-of-practice platforms with the latest research and data findings.Assist in the development: of new or ongoing initiatives, including review of policy literature in respect to the subject to enhance UNDP programming in the relevant field within the Arab Region.Document good practices: Including cases studies, innovations and pilot models for wider dissemination and sharing.Concept notes: Prepare conceptual framework / concept notes on new areas of work or development challenges.

Competencies

Functional Competencies

Strong sense of collaborative work, excellent communication and interpersonal skills;Keen attention to detail;Proven record of interest and work in the development field;Excellent analytical and research skills using state of the art quantitative analytical tools such as STATA, R;Research experience;Interest in the Arab States region and possibly some background in researching the region;

Professionalism

Demonstrated problem-solving skills and judgment in applying technical expertise to resolve a wide range of complex issues/problems;Ability to negotiate and to influence others to reach agreement;Ability to work under pressure;Shows pride in work and in achievement;Demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter, especially economic development and resilience;Is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results;Is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns;Shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges;Remains calm in stressful situations;Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work;Takes responsibility for incorporating the perspective of youth and ensuring the equal participation of young people as in all areas of work.

Communication

Speaks and writes clearly, concisely and effectively;Listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately;Asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication;Tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience;Demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed.

Teamwork

Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise;Is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda;Supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position;Shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings.

Planning & Organizing

Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies;Identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required;Allocates appropriate amount of time and resource for completing work;Foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning;Monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary;Uses time efficiently.

Accountability

Takes ownership of all responsibilities and honor commitments;Delivers outputs for which one has responsibility within prescribed time, cost and quality standards;Operates in compliance with organizational regulations and rules;Supports subordinates, provide oversight and take responsibility for delegated assignments;Takes personal responsibility for his/her own shortcomings and those of the work unit, where applicable.

Creativity

Actively seeks to improve program or services;Offers new and different options to solve problems or meet client needs;Promotes and persuades others to consider new ideas;Takes calculated risks on new and unusual ideas;Thinks “outside the box”;Takes an interest in new ideas and new ways of doing things;Not bound by current thinking or traditional approaches.

Technological Awareness

Keeps abreast of available technology;Understands applicability and limitation of technology to the work of the office;Actively seeks to apply technology to appropriate tasks;Shows willingness to learn new technology.

Education

Required Skills and Experience

Applicants to the UNDP internship programme must at the time of application meet one of the following requirements:

 Be enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme (such as a master’s programme, or higher) in subjects relevant to the work of Inclusive Growth Team (economics, development studies, public policy, international development and related fields).  Be enrolled in the final academic year of a first university degree programme (such as bachelor’s degree or equivalent) in subjects mentioned under (1) above.  Have recently graduated with a university degree (as defined in (1) and (2) above) and, if selected, must start the internship within one-year of graduation.  Be enrolled in a postgraduate professional traineeship program and undertake the internship as part of this program. 

Experience

Experience with quantitative data analysis using software like R, Stata, or Python is a strong asset.Demonstrated ability to work well both independently and within a multicultural team.Good command of information and communication technology.

Languages

Fluency in English (both oral and written) is required. Arabic and French language skills would be an asset but not necessary for the assignment.

Stipend

Where an intern is not financially supported by any institution or programme, such as a university, government, foundation or scholarship programme, a stipend intended to help cover basic daily expenses related to the internship, such as meals and transportation at the duty station, must be paid by the receiving office.The monthly amount of the stipend will be determined for each duty station based on the stipend rates published yearly by the OHR Policy and Compensation Unit. The stipend will be paid on a monthly basis and part-time internship arrangements are prorated accordingly.Where an intern is financially supported by an institution, government or third party, UNDP will, subject to the rules of such institution, government or third party, pay the intern the difference, if any, between the external financial support provided and the applicable UNDP stipend.No other payments of any kind will be made to an intern by the office in connection with an internship agreement.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Data Privacy

Please click here to view UNDP Data Privacy Statement

rows.title: Model Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
About Eip

Energy Infrastructure Partners LLC (EIP) is a minority-owned business specializing in energy efficiency, electrification, decarbonization, and demand-side management programs. With offices in New York, Illinois, California, Oregon, Pennsylvania, and Washington, EIP combines national reach with local market understanding. Our work advances sustainable energy solutions, supports economic development, and prioritizes benefits for disadvantaged communities. As a leader in clean energy program implementation and consulting, EIP is proud to help clients achieve meaningful environmental and economic outcomes through innovative, high-impact projects.

Position Description

EIP is seeking a Model Analyst based in Chicago to conduct regression analysis and quantify energy savings for strategic energy management (SEM) programs serving ComEd, PECO, and NYSEG markets. The analyst will build and maintain facility-level energy use models that account for production, weather, occupancy, and other relevant drivers, then use those models to assess changes in performance over time.

Working with engineers, SEM coaches, program managers, and customer teams, the Model Analyst will gather and validate data, select appropriate model variables and time periods, establish baselines, calculate normalized savings, and prepare documentation that supports program reporting and technical review. The role requires careful statistical analysis and the judgment to distinguish meaningful operational improvements from data issues or changes in facility activity.

The ideal candidate can explain modeling assumptions and results clearly to technical and nontechnical colleagues, manage recurring analyses for multiple facilities, and adapt methods to each utility program’s measurement and verification requirements.

Objectives of this Role

Reliable Energy Baselines: Develop reproducible regression models that describe normal facility energy use and its relationship to relevant operating conditions. Defensible Savings Estimates: Quantify changes in energy use attributable to SEM activities using approved methods, documented adjustments, and appropriate uncertainty checks. Data Quality: Identify missing, inconsistent, or anomalous utility and driver data before they affect model results or savings claims. Program Compliance: Apply the applicable utility and program measurement and verification protocols consistently across participating facilities. Actionable Insight: Translate model findings into useful feedback for SEM coaches, engineers, customers, and program managers. Timely Delivery: Maintain models and recurring reports on schedule while supporting accurate portfolio-level tracking and continuous improvement. 

Daily and Monthly Responsibilities

Assemble Analysis Data: Collect and organize utility bills, interval meter data, production records, weather data, operating schedules, occupancy, and other drivers relevant to each facility. Validate Data Quality: Check units, time stamps, meter coverage, missing periods, duplicate records, outliers, and changes in operations; document corrections and unresolved limitations. Develop Regression Models: Select appropriate baseline periods and independent variables; build and test facility-level models using suitable statistical tools and program-approved methods. Evaluate Model Performance: Review residuals, explanatory power, bias, error metrics, and the plausibility of coefficients; investigate poor model fit and avoid unsupported savings conclusions. Calculate SEM Savings: Compare observed reporting-period energy use with modeled baseline consumption adjusted to reporting-period conditions; document formulas, inputs, and results. Address Facility Changes: Assess whether equipment, production, schedules, occupancy, or other non-routine changes require model revisions or documented adjustments under program rules. Support Measurement and Verification: Prepare model files, data dictionaries, calculation workbooks, charts, and narratives for internal review, utility reporting, and evaluator requests. Collaborate with Program Teams: Work with SEM coaches and engineers to understand facility operations, validate model drivers, investigate unexpected trends, and interpret results. Communicate Findings: Present baselines, performance trends, savings estimates, assumptions, and uncertainty in concise reports and visualizations suited to the intended audience. Maintain Portfolio Tracking: Update recurring analyses, track analysis status and due dates, reconcile facility results to program reporting, and escalate data or modeling risks. Improve Analytical Practices: Help refine templates, quality checks, documentation standards, and repeatable workflows across SEM programs. 

Required Qualifications

Education: Bachelor’s degree in engineering, statistics, mathematics, data science, economics, physics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent relevant experience. Regression Analysis: Demonstrated ability to develop, interpret, and validate multivariable regression models using real-world time-series or operational data. Data Analysis Tools: Strong Excel skills and proficiency with at least one analytical environment such as R, Python, SQL, or a comparable statistical tool. Analytical Judgment: Ability to assess model fit, data quality, variable selection, outliers, seasonality, and uncertainty without relying solely on automated outputs. Technical Documentation: Ability to maintain transparent calculations and explain methods, assumptions, adjustments, and results clearly in writing. Collaboration: Ability to work with engineers, customer-facing teams, and program managers to understand the operational context behind the data. Organization: Ability to manage analyses for multiple facilities and programs, maintain version control, and meet recurring reporting deadlines. 

Preferred Qualifications

SEM Experience: Experience developing energy baselines or calculating savings for strategic energy management, industrial energy management, or related utility programs. Measurement and Verification: Familiarity with whole-facility measurement and verification, normalized metered energy consumption approaches, IPMVP Option C, or utility-specific SEM protocols. Energy Data: Experience working with utility interval data, billing data, weather normalization, industrial production data, or building management system trends. Statistical Methods: Experience evaluating model bias, normalized mean bias error, coefficient of variation of root mean squared error, confidence intervals, or comparable model quality measures where appropriate. Energy Systems: Familiarity with commercial or industrial energy systems and common factors that influence facility energy consumption. Program Markets: Experience supporting ComEd, PECO, NYSEG, or other utility energy efficiency programs. 

WE OFFER

Competitive base salary commensurate with experience and qualifications. ($60k-$75k)Performance-based bonus tied to individual and company performance. 401(k) retirement savings plan with employer match. Comprehensive health, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance. Paid vacation, sick time, and holidays. Professional development and training opportunities. A dynamic, inclusive work environment that encourages collaboration, innovation, and growth. 

Join us!

At EIP, your analysis will help organizations see whether changes in how they operate are producing measurable energy savings. You will bring statistical rigor and practical judgment to SEM programs across multiple utility markets.

Energy Infrastructure Partners is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Note: This is a Chicago-based hybrid position. EIP generally requires four days per week in office when not traveling. Specific in-office requirements will be based on program needs.

EIP does not offer visa sponsorship for this position.

rows.title: Machine Learning Engineer, Applied

parsed.text: New York City, NY, United States

rows.descriptionText:
About Trace

Trace Labs is building the data infrastructure for physical AI.

Physical AI has the potential to transform how work gets done in the real world, from robotics to embodied systems that can see, move, and interact with their environment. But today, progress is held back by one big gap: there’s no scalable way to collect high-quality, real-world training data. Frontier robotics models are trained on far less data than language models, because there’s no “internet of robotics data.”

Trace exists to change that. We capture how humans actually interact with the physical world, at scale, and we build the ML systems that make every hour of that data more valuable.

We’re an early, deeply technical team. We move fast, we care about quality, and we believe the teams with the best data will build the best robots.

The role

This role sits between ML engineering and research. You’ll bring strong ML engineering skills, a research mindset, and deep learning fundamentals to the hardest problems we see coming at Trace, then ship the answers into production.

You’ll work closely with our computer vision team, but this role is broader and more product-focused. You won’t live on one type of data. One month you might be working with sensor signals, the next with hand tracking video, the next with language. What matters is getting a high-quality model working fast and putting it to use.

We care much more about what you’ve built and shipped than where you’ve published. If you’re earlier in your career but have a clear track record of moving fast and owning hard problems, we want to talk.

What You Will Do

Own models end to end: data, training, evaluation, and deployment into our annotation pipeline. Build training pipelines for large, multimodal datasets, including video, sensor streams, and language. Partner with our Head of Engineering and the CV team to get models into production and keep them improving. Start with the simplest approach that works, then make it better. Pull from recent papers when they help you ship, not as the end goal. Move quickly between very different problems, and build the tooling you need along the way. 

What we're looking for

A BS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, Aerospace, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. An MS is a plus, not a must. 2+ years of industry of hands-on experience training deep learning models on real-world data, at a company, startup, or national lab. Earlier in your career is okay if your track record shows it. Strong proficiency in Python and a modern deep learning framework such as PyTorch or JAX. A solid grounding in ML fundamentals, including architectures, optimization, loss design, and evaluation. Comfort with messy, real-world data such as video, time series, or sensor streams. An extraordinary bias toward shipping. You go from idea to working model fast, and you make good calls under uncertainty. High agency. You find the problem, own it, and get it done without waiting to be told. Range. You’re excited to work across different kinds of data and problems, not just one narrow specialty. 

Why Trace Labs

A foundational problem. The data layer for physical AI is still being defined. You’ll help define it. Data at scale from day one. We have the resources to collect it. Your job is to make it count. Real ownership. Your models ship into production and directly shape what our data can do. Room to grow. Go deeper into ML, take on bigger systems, or both. 

Compensation Range: $185K - $245K
