rows.title: Research Fellow
rows.descriptionText:
Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Biostatistics and Cancer Genetics

Department of Data Science, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute

Dana-Farber Cancer Institute (DFCI) is seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Biostatistics to join the Department of Data Science and contribute to collaborative research in cancer genetics and precision oncology.

The primary focus of this position is collaborative and applied biostatistical research. The fellow will work closely with clinical investigators, geneticists, genetic counselors, computational researchers, and biostatisticians on study design, data management and derivation, statistical analysis, interpretation, and scientific communication. The fellow will also have opportunities to contribute to methodological research motivated by the scientific projects.

Approximately 50% of the fellow’s effort will be devoted to an NIH-funded R01 project focused on the development and validation of prediction models for identifying germline pathogenic variants, using large multi-institutional datasets from Dana-Farber and collaborating cancer centers. The remaining 50% will support collaborative research within the Division of Cancer Genetics and Prevention at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

Located in Boston and the surrounding communities, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute is a leader in life changing breakthroughs in cancer research and patient care. We are united in our mission of conquering cancer, HIV/AIDS, and related diseases. We strive to create an inclusive, diverse, and equitable environment where we provide compassionate and comprehensive care to patients of all backgrounds, and design programs to promote public health particularly among high-risk and underserved populations. We conduct groundbreaking research that advances treatment, we educate tomorrow's physician/researchers, and we work with amazing partners, including other Harvard Medical School-affiliated hospitals.

Responsibilities

NIH-Funded R01 Project — Approximately 50% Effort

The Fellow Will Serve As a Biostatistician On a Multidisciplinary Team Developing And Validating Statistical Prediction Models For Germline Pathogenic Variants. Responsibilities Will Include:

Conducting statistical analyses of large clinical, genetic, and genomic datasets.Performing data derivation, data cleaning, harmonization, quality control, and integration of data from multiple institutions and data sources.Developing and validating statistical prediction models.Evaluating model discrimination, calibration, clinical utility, and performance across patient subgroups and institutions.Conducting simulation studies and computational evaluations.Contributing to the development and evaluation of statistical methods motivated by the project.Developing reproducible statistical programs and analysis workflows.Preparing statistical results, tables, and figures for manuscripts, presentations, and scientific reports.Contributing to peer-reviewed manuscripts and other scientific publications.

Collaborative Cancer Genetics Research — Approximately 50% Effort

The fellow will also serve as a collaborative biostatistician for research conducted within the DFCI cancer genetics program. The fellow will collaborate with clinical investigators, geneticists, genetic counselors, and other research team members on clinical, translational, and observational studies in cancer genetics, hereditary cancer, and cancer prevention.

Responsibilities Will Include:

Providing statistical input on study design and research questions.Developing statistical analysis plans.Performing data management, data derivation, and statistical analyses.Selecting and applying appropriate statistical methods for clinical and biomedical research.Interpreting statistical results in collaboration with investigators.Preparing tables, figures, and statistical summaries.Contributing to manuscripts, abstracts, presentations, and grant applications.Participating in multidisciplinary research meetings and communicating statistical concepts clearly to clinical and scientific collaborators.Managing multiple collaborative projects and working effectively with investigators and research staff.

Qualifications

Required

PhD or equivalent doctoral degree in Biostatistics at the time of appointment.Strong training in applied biostatistical methods.Experience with regression modeling and other statistical methods commonly used in clinical or biomedical research.Strong statistical programming skills, preferably in R.Experience using Git and GitHub/GitLab for version control and collaborative development of reproducible statistical code and analysis workflows.Experience with data management, data derivation, and statistical analysis of clinical or biomedical datasets.Ability to independently conduct statistical analyses from preparation of analysis-ready datasets through interpretation and presentation of results.Strong written and verbal communication skills.Interest in collaborative biomedical research and multidisciplinary teamwork.

Preferred

Experience with prediction modeling, statistical learning, penalized regression, or related methods.Experience analyzing large observational, clinical, genetic, genomic, or other complex biomedical datasets.Experience working with data from multiple sources or institutions.Experience with simulation studies or computational evaluation of statistical methods.Experience contributing statistical analyses and interpretation to peer-reviewed biomedical manuscripts.Familiarity with cancer research, genetic epidemiology, cancer genetics, or genomic data analysis is desirable but not required.

At Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, we work every day to create an innovative, caring, and inclusive environment where every patient, family, and staff member feels they belong. As relentless as we are in our mission to reduce the burden of cancer for all, we are committed to having faculty and staff who offer multifaceted experiences. Cancer knows no boundaries and when it comes to hiring the most dedicated and compassionate professionals, neither do we. If working in this kind of organization inspires you, we encourage you to apply.

Dana-Farber Cancer Institute is an equal opportunity employer and affirms the right of every qualified applicant to receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, national origin, sexual orientation, genetic information, disability, age, ancestry, military service, protected veteran status, or other characteristics protected by law.

rows.title: Associate Data Scientist, DIBI
rows.descriptionText:
About The Opportunity

JOB SUMMARY

The Defense Industrial Base Institute at Northeastern University (NU) – a rapidly growing defense focused institute that conducts cutting-edge applied R&D – is seeking an experienced and highly capable Jr. Data Scientist with expertise in applying methods/frameworks/systems that apply ML&AI. The Jr. Data Scientist will operate as part of a multi-disciplinary team (academia, industry and government) and will contribute directly to the successful execution of federally funded projects/activities,

Responsibilities include providing technical expertise and analytical support to Principal investigators or co-principal investigators as a Jr. Data Scientist for a wide range of projects and activities involving machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI), including autonomy, sensing and communication, and decision support systems, among others. The Jr, Data Scientist will work collaboratively with and help guide, multi-disciplinary teams across the DIBI Higher Education Consortium — spanning academic, government, and industry partners — to design, validate, and maintain datasets and analytical products that inform institute leadership and sponsor decision-making. Specifically, the Jr. Data Scientist will take a role in building and maintaining the data pipelines and analytical components underlying the existing Navigator methodology, working closely with — and providing guidance to — data researchers, engineers, and leadership across the institute.

Successful candidates will be responsible team players and passionate about machine learning technologies, as well as possess a deep understanding of machine learning technology and experience in turning machine learning systems into practical, state-of-the-art systems that can be enhanced for projects or activities as per federal agency. A close working relationship with the team, along with creative thinking on the application of the Navigator framework for government and industry contracts, will be required.

The primary office for this position is located at NU’s Boston Campus Through NU, the institute offers an impressive benefits package, including multiple retirement plan options with extremely generous matching, as well as tuition waiver for classes and advanced degree programs. A full description of available benefits can be found on the NU website.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Education & Experience

Required

Master’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related field 2–4 years of professional experience in software engineering, data science, or applied R&D, with exposure to machine learning and AI system development in research, prototype, or production environments.


Preferred

Master’s degree or Ph.D with a focus on data science, data‑intensive systems, network science, optimization, or related areas.Experience contributing to government, defense, or security‑related R&D programs (internships, fellowships, or full‑time roles).Familiarity with simulation‑based models (e.g., physics‑based, network‑based, agent‑based, or stochastic simulations) for analysis, experimentation, or decision support.undefined 


Required

Skills & Attributes

Advanced proficiency in Python and/or R studio and familiarity with modern ML/AI development workflows.Exposure to C++ and/or Java for performance‑critical components Experience contributing to the design, implementation, testing, or evaluation of ML/AI-enabled or simulation-drive software systems.Demonstrated experience with data visualization and reporting tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI, matplotlib, Plotly), including designing dashboards for executive or sponsor audiences.Proven experience independently building, validating, and interpreting statistical or machine learning models, and communicating tradeoffs to non-technical stakeholders.Strong command of data cleaning, ETL processes, and data quality assurance practices, including for messy or incomplete real-world datasets.Solid software engineering fundamentals, including version control (e.g., Git/GitHub), documentation, and reproducibility.Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience presenting analytical findings directly to leadership or sponsors.U.S. Citizenship with the ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance


Desired:

 Exposure to Retrieval‑Augmented Generation (RAG), vector databases, embedding pipelines, or LLM‑enabled systems.Familiarity with cloud computing environments (e.g., Azure, AWS or GovCloud equivalents).Introductory experience with graph‑based ML or GNNs is a plusMonte Carlo or stochastic simulation methodsSynthetic data generation or simulation‑in‑the‑loop workflowsFamiliarity with geospatial data, spatiotemporal datasets, or PostgreSQL/PostGIS is a plus. Interest in UI or frontend development for technical or analyst‑facing tools (e.g., Svelte, React, or similar frameworks).Exposure to dashboarding or BI tools for analyst-facing or leadership-facing reportingFamiliarity with MLOps concepts, experiment tracking, or reproducible research pipelines.Experience working with multidisciplinary teams across research, engineering, and applied R&D environments.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES & ACCOUNTABILITIES

Support Research and Development efforts to scale Navigator methodology applied to defense contracts (SIB), to include, development and implementation, prototype modeling & simulation, design, and experimentation. This supports the defense funding received that supports this role (40%)

Test and validation of soAI/ML Tools for sprints, tasks, projects and deliverables; to include scaling of projects by suggesting tools and systems that enhance efficiency and support humans in their work (40%)

Provide subject matter expertise across a diverse set of application areas and ad hoc requests that may come in from the sponsor. Present information and answer questions form government sponsors and stakeholders.Research and support PI or CO-PIs with scoping project budgets as appropriate (Systems, tools) (10%)

Special Projects as assigned: Working closely with Managing Director, Founding Director and other core leadership members, help to scope proposals and opportunities. Working closely with DIBI Leadership Team and Sr. Director, Strategy and Communications to make recommendations on systems build out for internal operations (10%)

Position Type

Research

Additional Information

Northeastern University considers factors such as candidate work experience, education and skills when extending an offer.

Northeastern has a comprehensive benefits package for benefit eligible employees. This includes medical, vision, dental, paid time off, tuition assistance, wellness & life, retirement- as well as commuting & transportation. Visit https://hr.northeastern.edu/benefits/ for more information.

All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, age, sex, sexual orientation, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) 

Waystone is seeking a clinician who is a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) to support adults aged 22 and older with intellectual and developmental disabilities (I/DD), including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), acquired brain injury (ABI), and dementia or memory loss within residential programs.

At Waystone, we foster an environment where both our team and the individuals we serve can thrive. Our group homes provide a slower-paced setting that allows clinicians to focus on individualized care, build meaningful connections, and deliver thoughtful, person-centered support— without the fast-paced demands of traditional clinical settings.

Location: As a clinician, you will work across multiple residential programs (group homes) in the Merrimack Valley, with primary assignments in Methuen and Haverhill. Mileage will be reimbursed in accordance with company policy for travel between program locations. 

Schedule: Monday - Friday 8:00am - 4:00pm. Some flexibility may be allowed with prior supervisory approval. This position is benefit eligible as of the date of hire.

Health, Dental, and Vision insurance, eligible to enroll on your first day! Deliver direct counseling and behavioral support, tailored to individual needs. Model and train staff to implement behavioral strategies and protocols effectively. Design and oversee behavioral plans, including PBS plans, restrictive interventions, and biopsychosocial approaches, supported by consistent data collection and reporting. Master’s degree in psychology, Social Work or related field. Currently licensed as a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) or eligible for certification within six months of hire. Waystone Health & Human Services is a 501c3, nonprofit, human services organization supporting youth and adults with intellectual, developmental, and physical disabilities; acquired brain injuries; and mental health diagnoses. rows.title: Finance Associate - Corporate Finance
rows.descriptionText:
Bain Capital Overview

Bain Capital, LP is one of the world’s leading private multi-asset alternative investment firms with approximately $225 billion of assets under management that creates lasting impact for our investors, teams, businesses, and the communities in which we live. Since our founding in 1984, we’ve applied our insight and experience to organically expand into several asset classes including private equity, credit, public equity, venture capital and real estate. We leverage our shared platform to capture cross-asset class opportunities in strategic areas of focus. With offices on four continents, our global team aligns our interests with those of our investors for lasting impact.

CORPORATE FINANCE GROUP

The Corporate Finance Group consists of 25 individuals and is responsible for the day-to-day accounting for the Global Management Company. Our general ledger and enterprise resource planning (ERP) platform is Workday Financials. The Global Management Company consolidates the operations of the Investment Advisors (one for each business: Private Equity, Credit, Ventures, Public Equity, Double Impact, Life Sciences, Real Estate, and Partnership Strategies) and the entities by geography including Asia Pacific (Hong Kong, Tokyo, Shanghai, and Australia), Europe (London, Dublin, Munich and South Africa) and India (Mumbai and Mauritius). The Corporate Finance Group is also responsible for tax accounting and works closely with the Tax Department on Tax Reporting. Various other responsibilities within the group include the treasury and cash management function, internal reporting, external reporting, accounts receivable, accounts payable and fixed assets.

Position Description

The Finance Associate will join a structured program across the Accounts Payable (AP) and Accounts Receivable (AR) functions of the Global Management Company. The position is designed to give the Associate end-to-end exposure to how money moves through the firm: supplier invoices, employee expense reimbursement, and corporate payments on the AP side, and the billing, collection, and reimbursement of deal, fund, and portfolio company expenses on the AR side.

Together, AP and AR capture every dollar the business spends and every dollar it recovers from external parties. Because all of this activity posts to the general ledger through Workday, the Associate will develop a detailed working knowledge of the journal-level data that drives the firm's accounting, close, and reporting processes.

The Associate will have exposure to both functions and will have the opportunity to take on broader Corporate Finance responsibilities (quarter-end close, reporting, treasury) as performance allows. We are looking for someone who is smart, capable, and comfortable in a fast-paced, high-volume environment where accuracy and timeliness both matter.

Key Responsibilities

Accounts Payable

 Process third-party supplier invoices end-to-end: receipt and intake, verification of financial data and required audit attributes, coordination of approvals, and facilitation of payment Review invoice coding and payment details in partnership with the Accounting and Reporting Team to ensure accuracy and completeness of financial data for each invoice Prepare, send, and properly record wires and other payments for supplier invoices Support the processing and review of employee expense reports, procurement card transactions, and ad hoc bank transactions, ensuring each is appropriately coded, approved, and recorded Research, resolve, and respond to inquiries regarding invoices, including payment status, invoice attributes, and policy and process questions Coordinate audit and processing tasks with our external service provider and offshore processing team Support period-end AP cutoff and assist with quarter-end account reconciliations as part of the quarterly close

Accounts Receivable

 Prepare quarterly management fee and expense reimbursement invoices for portfolio companies managed by Bain Capital, LP's business units, as well as expense summaries for pending deals Prepare invoices to Business Units throughout the year and record the related revenue and expense reimbursements in the general ledger Monitor amounts billed versus collected from portfolio companies and funds, and support the collections and external reporting process Assist in monitoring compliance with firm policies and contractual agreements governing the billing of expenses to external parties, and in monitoring the allocation of spend across funds an Business Units Maintain the accuracy and completeness of accounts receivable records, including aging analysis and reconciliation of customer invoice activity to the general ledger

General

 Interact with stakeholders across the organization, including Business Unit Finance Teams, Legal, Tax, and Compliance Use Workday reporting (e.g., journal line, supplier invoice, and receivables aging reports) and Excel to support reconciliations, tie-outs, and management reporting Contribute to system improvements and process enhancements, including the use of AI and automation tools to streamline recurring work, and help document and refine procedures as the role evolves Assist with ad hoc projects and analysis as needed

General Qualifications

 Detail-oriented, organized, and professional Strong work ethic, hands-on approach, and a desire to learn Strong time management skills, with the ability to prioritize competing responsibilities and work under tight deadlines Solid problem-solving skills and sound judgment Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced, high-volume environment with an emphasis on accuracy and timeliness Strong interpersonal and communication skills, both verbal and written, with the ability to interact with outside parties and personnel at all levels of the organization Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Excel skills (formulas, lookups, pivot tables, shortcuts) Workday Financials experience is a plus but not required

DESIRED BACKGROUND

 Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance required, with a minimum GPA of 3.3 0–2 years of related experience; general accounting experience and/or coursework is important Exposure to AI tools (e.g., Claude), SQL, Python, or other automation and data tools is a plus

Compensation:

Expected Annual Base Salary $70,000 – 75,000

Actual base salary will be determined by a wide range of factors including but not limited to role, function, level, experience, qualifications and geographic location. In addition to a competitive base salary, this position may be eligible for a discretionary annual bonus based upon factors such as individual impact, team and firm performance. Bain Capital offers a competitive benefits package designed to support employees’ health, financial security, family needs, and overall well-being.

Bain Capital is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status.

The GRC Analyst role is pivotal in safeguarding the organization’s assets, maintaining compliance with regulatory standards, and enhancing overall governance practices.

This role follows a hybrid schedule and requires regular, in-person work at our Boston, MA or Hampton, NH office. Our hybrid model is M/T/W in office and TH/F are optional work-from-home.  Perks

The salary for MA-based and NH-based employees hired into this role will be aligned with the range below. This is a good faith estimate, and the amount of base salary will correspond with a candidate’s professional experience, qualifications and internal equity.

rows.title: Marketing and Merchandising Coordinator
rows.descriptionText:
Company OverviewAt Tee Commerce, we make it easy for private clubs and golf courses to sell merchandise online with no extra work or inventory risk. We design and manage custom online retail storefronts that match each club’s look and feel, giving members access to hundreds of products from top brands. As orders come in, we handle fulfillment, applying the club’s logo and ensuring a seamless shopping experience. Our team also manages inventory, customer service, sourcing new merchandise, and marketing, allowing clubs to expand their retail offerings without added complexity. Joining our team means becoming part of a fast-growing startup in the golf industry where every role directly impacts our success.
Job SummaryAs our Marketing and Merchandising Coordinator, you’ll help our partner clubs get more out of their online stores – both by shaping what shoppers see and by helping plan the promotions that drive them to buy. You’ll partner closely with the Customer Success and Product teams to strategize seasonal promotions, marketing calendars, and campaigns for our partner clubs, then bring those plans to life by creating the content – emails, social posts, graphics, and on-site messaging – needed to execute them.
On the merchandising side, you’ll help decide what each storefront features and how it’s laid out: curating collections, spotlighting seasonal or high-margin products, and refining storefront layout and navigation to increase sales and average order value. You’ll also support the health of our product catalog – keeping listings, descriptions, images, and categorization accurate and up to date – so our merchandising strategy is always built on a clean, well-organized foundation.
This is a hands-on, cross-functional role for someone who’s equally comfortable thinking strategically about what will sell and rolling up their sleeves to build the campaign, curate the collection, or clean up the catalog that makes it happen.
Key Responsibilities● Partner with the Customer Success team to plan promotional calendars, campaigns, and marketing initiatives for partner clubs, aligned to seasonality, inventory, and each club’s goals.● Create the marketing content: needed to execute those plans – email campaigns, social media posts, promotional graphics, product photography, and on-site banners and messaging.● Strategically merchandise partner storefronts by selecting and curating featured products and collections, and refining storefront layout and navigation to increase sales and average order value.● Analyze storefront and campaign performance (best sellers, conversion, engagement) to inform merchandising and content decisions, and iterate based on results.● Maintain and support the product catalog: adding new products, writing product descriptions, sourcing and optimizing images, and keeping categorization and tagging clean and consistent.● Collaborate with Customer Success on seasonal launches (new season, holiday, tournament merchandise) to ensure storefronts are stocked, styled, and promoted on time.● Stay on top of merchandising and e-commerce best practices, bringing recommendations back to the team on how to improve storefront performance.● Support the broader Customer Success and Sales teams with ad hoc marketing materials – sales collateral, one-pagers, and social content – as needed.
Qualifications & Skills● 1–3+ years of experience in marketing, e-commerce merchandising, content creation, or a related role – ideally at a retail, e-commerce, or DTC brand.● Strong eye for visual merchandising and storefront design; comfortable deciding what to feature and how to lay it out to drive sales.● Hands-on content creation skills – comfortable with tools like Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, or similar for graphics, plus basic photography and photo editing.● Excellent writing skills for marketing copy, product descriptions, and campaign content.● Detail-oriented and organized; comfortable managing a product catalog and keeping data clean across many storefronts.● Comfortable working in e-commerce platforms (Shopify experience a plus) and reading basic performance analytics.● Self-starter who can move fluidly between strategic planning and hands-on execution.
Benefits & Perks● Compensation: Base $65–75k ● Hybrid Work Environment: Ability for a mix of working at home and in the office to be discussed with the manager during the interview process.● Startup Culture: Join a collaborative, fast-paced environment where your contributions directly impact the company’s success.● Growth Path: As an early hire in this function, you’ll help define our marketing and merchandising playbook as Tee Commerce scales.● Passion for Golf? Even Better! If you love golf or have an interest in the industry, this is a great opportunity to work with top clubs and golf professionals.

Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Biostatistics and Cancer Genetics

Department of Data Science, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute

Dana-Farber Cancer Institute (DFCI) is seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Biostatistics to join the Department of Data Science and contribute to collaborative research in cancer genetics and precision oncology.

The primary focus of this position is collaborative and applied biostatistical research. The fellow will work closely with clinical investigators, geneticists, genetic counselors, computational researchers, and biostatisticians on study design, data management and derivation, statistical analysis, interpretation, and scientific communication. The fellow will also have opportunities to contribute to methodological research motivated by the scientific projects.

Approximately 50% of the fellow’s effort will be devoted to an NIH-funded R01 project focused on the development and validation of prediction models for identifying germline pathogenic variants, using large multi-institutional datasets from Dana-Farber and collaborating cancer centers. The remaining 50% will support collaborative research within the Division of Cancer Genetics and Prevention at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

Located in Boston and the surrounding communities, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute is a leader in life changing breakthroughs in cancer research and patient care. We are united in our mission of conquering cancer, HIV/AIDS, and related diseases. We strive to create an inclusive, diverse, and equitable environment where we provide compassionate and comprehensive care to patients of all backgrounds, and design programs to promote public health particularly among high-risk and underserved populations. We conduct groundbreaking research that advances treatment, we educate tomorrow's physician/researchers, and we work with amazing partners, including other Harvard Medical School-affiliated hospitals.

Responsibilities

NIH-Funded R01 Project — Approximately 50% Effort

The Fellow Will Serve As a Biostatistician On a Multidisciplinary Team Developing And Validating Statistical Prediction Models For Germline Pathogenic Variants. Responsibilities Will Include:

Conducting statistical analyses of large clinical, genetic, and genomic datasets.Performing data derivation, data cleaning, harmonization, quality control, and integration of data from multiple institutions and data sources.Developing and validating statistical prediction models.Evaluating model discrimination, calibration, clinical utility, and performance across patient subgroups and institutions.Conducting simulation studies and computational evaluations.Contributing to the development and evaluation of statistical methods motivated by the project.Developing reproducible statistical programs and analysis workflows.Preparing statistical results, tables, and figures for manuscripts, presentations, and scientific reports.Contributing to peer-reviewed manuscripts and other scientific publications.

Collaborative Cancer Genetics Research — Approximately 50% Effort

The fellow will also serve as a collaborative biostatistician for research conducted within the DFCI cancer genetics program. The fellow will collaborate with clinical investigators, geneticists, genetic counselors, and other research team members on clinical, translational, and observational studies in cancer genetics, hereditary cancer, and cancer prevention.

Responsibilities Will Include:

Providing statistical input on study design and research questions.Developing statistical analysis plans.Performing data management, data derivation, and statistical analyses.Selecting and applying appropriate statistical methods for clinical and biomedical research.Interpreting statistical results in collaboration with investigators.Preparing tables, figures, and statistical summaries.Contributing to manuscripts, abstracts, presentations, and grant applications.Participating in multidisciplinary research meetings and communicating statistical concepts clearly to clinical and scientific collaborators.Managing multiple collaborative projects and working effectively with investigators and research staff.

Qualifications

Required

PhD or equivalent doctoral degree in Biostatistics at the time of appointment.Strong training in applied biostatistical methods.Experience with regression modeling and other statistical methods commonly used in clinical or biomedical research.Strong statistical programming skills, preferably in R.Experience using Git and GitHub/GitLab for version control and collaborative development of reproducible statistical code and analysis workflows.Experience with data management, data derivation, and statistical analysis of clinical or biomedical datasets.Ability to independently conduct statistical analyses from preparation of analysis-ready datasets through interpretation and presentation of results.Strong written and verbal communication skills.Interest in collaborative biomedical research and multidisciplinary teamwork.

Preferred

Experience with prediction modeling, statistical learning, penalized regression, or related methods.Experience analyzing large observational, clinical, genetic, genomic, or other complex biomedical datasets.Experience working with data from multiple sources or institutions.Experience with simulation studies or computational evaluation of statistical methods.Experience contributing statistical analyses and interpretation to peer-reviewed biomedical manuscripts.Familiarity with cancer research, genetic epidemiology, cancer genetics, or genomic data analysis is desirable but not required.

At Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, we work every day to create an innovative, caring, and inclusive environment where every patient, family, and staff member feels they belong. As relentless as we are in our mission to reduce the burden of cancer for all, we are committed to having faculty and staff who offer multifaceted experiences. Cancer knows no boundaries and when it comes to hiring the most dedicated and compassionate professionals, neither do we. If working in this kind of organization inspires you, we encourage you to apply.

Dana-Farber Cancer Institute is an equal opportunity employer and affirms the right of every qualified applicant to receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, national origin, sexual orientation, genetic information, disability, age, ancestry, military service, protected veteran status, or other characteristics protected by law.

Dana-Farber Cancer Institute (DFCI) is seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Biostatistics to join the Department of Data Science and contribute to collaborative research in cancer genetics and precision oncology.

The primary focus of this position is collaborative and applied biostatistical research. The fellow will work closely with clinical investigators, geneticists, genetic counselors, computational researchers, and biostatisticians on study design, data management and derivation, statistical analysis, interpretation, and scientific communication. The fellow will also have opportunities to contribute to methodological research motivated by the scientific projects.

Approximately 50% of the fellow’s effort will be devoted to an NIH-funded R01 project focused on the development and validation of prediction models for identifying germline pathogenic variants, using large multi-institutional datasets from Dana-Farber and collaborating cancer centers. The remaining 50% will support collaborative research within the Division of Cancer Genetics and Prevention at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

Located in Boston and the surrounding communities, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute is a leader in life changing breakthroughs in cancer research and patient care. We strive to create an inclusive, diverse, and equitable environment where we provide compassionate and comprehensive care to patients of all backgrounds, and design programs to promote public health particularly among high-risk and underserved populations. We conduct groundbreaking research that advances treatment, we educate tomorrow's physician/researchers, and we work with amazing partners, including other Harvard Medical School-affiliated hospitals.

rows.title: ML Engineer
rows.descriptionText:
Machine Learning Engineer

About Proxima

Proxima (formerly VantAI) is advancing an AI-native approach to drug discovery by making protein interactions programmable. Our platform brings together foundation-model machine learning, a scalable data generation engine, and a partnership track record exceeding $5B in collaborations across the world’s leading biopharma and tech organizations. We’ve recently closed an oversubscribed seed round partnering us with an elite group of sophisticated and dedicated VCs including DCVC, Nvidia’s Nventures, AIX, and Yosemite among others.

Neo-1 is our all-atom foundation model that combines state-of-the-art structure prediction and molecular generation in a single system. Neo-1 enables rapid exploration of chemical and structural space for high-value, previously intractable targets, and in particular unlocks small molecule proximity therapeutics like molecular glues with AI for the first time.

In parallel, we are developing an advanced structural interactomics platform (NeoLink) built on proprietary XLMS technology and a lab equipped with next-generation mass spectrometry instrumentation. This platform produces proteome-scale maps of protein interactions and helps identify small molecules that modulate proximity. Together with Neo-1, it creates an integrated system capable of co-folding protein complexes while generating candidate small molecules to influence those interactions. Proximity-based therapeutics represent one of the most promising frontiers in modern drug discovery with the potential to treat previously intractable diseases and target ‘undruggable’ proteins. Our technology combines proteome-scale structural data with state-of-the-art generative AI foundation models and, coupled with our talented team of scientists and engineers, we are uniquely well-positioned to discover and develop a new class of medicines. Come join us!

About You

We are looking for a versatile software engineer to build the tools and systems behind our drug discovery research. You will work across automation, infrastructure, data, and ML, helping scientists develop models, run experiments, and use the results.

You enjoy taking a problem from investigation through deployment. Your work might involve integrating a dataset into training, diagnosing a stalled inference job, building an API for scientific results, or automating a manual workflow. You can find your way around an unfamiliar codebase, understand the constraints, and deliver a focused, well-tested improvement.

Our environment centers on Python and PyTorch, with containerized workloads, Kubernetes, cloud storage, and shared GPU compute. You will work closely with researchers and infrastructure engineers.

Relevant areas of expertise might include high-performance cloud computing, systems engineering, and machine learning, but specific knowledge of any of these areas is less critical than versatility and a willingness to learn and work anywhere in the tech stack. We value individuals who want to make an impact, have a deep intellectual curiosity, enjoy solving challenging problems, and have a track record of achievement.

Outcomes For This Role

Build reliable scientific workflows that colleagues can run, reproduce, and troubleshoot with less manual intervention.Integrate new models, datasets, and evaluation methods while preserving data correctness and compatibility with existing experiments.Improve compute workflows through better job submission, monitoring, failure recovery, and artifact tracking.Identify and remove bottlenecks in data preparation, execution, and evaluation so researchers can iterate faster.Deliver libraries, services, and developer tools that are easy to use and maintain, with appropriate tests, documentation, and monitoring.Contributing to the culture of a rapidly growing companyBeing challenged by your colleagues and learning something new every day

Specific Skills And Qualifications

Strong Python and software engineering fundamentals, including data structures, interface design, testing, concurrency, and systematic debugging.A track record of delivering software that other people use and depend on, including maintaining and troubleshooting it after release.Experience building or supporting ML or scientific computing workflows, with an understanding of how data, model execution, and evaluation fit together. PyTorch experience is a must.Experience running software on Linux, working with containers, and shipping changes through automated tests and CI/CD.Ability to break down ambiguous problems, make progress independently, and explain technical tradeoffs with evidence.Willingness to work across automation, infrastructure, data, and ML, with a strong sense of ownership and clear communication with scientists and engineers.Ability to use AI development tools effectively and take responsibility for the correctness and maintainability of the resulting code.

Experience with Kubernetes, cloud platforms, workflow orchestration, databases, or computational biology and chemistry is valuable. We welcome strong engineers from other technical domains; a biology or chemistry background is not required.

Introduction

At IBM Software, we transform client challenges into solutions. Building the world’s leading AI-powered, cloud-native products that shape the future of business and society. Our legacy of innovation creates endless opportunities for IBMers to learn, grow, and make an impact on a global scale. Working in Software means joining a team fueled by curiosity and collaboration. You’ll work with diverse technologies, partners, and industries to design, develop, and deliver solutions that power digital transformation. With a culture that values innovation, growth, and continuous learning, IBM Software places you at the heart of IBM’s product and technology landscape. Here, you’ll have the tools and opportunities to advance your career while creating software that changes the world.

Your Role And Responsibilities

This is a 16‑week Co‑Op position designed for actively enrolled undergraduate students who are interested in gaining hands‑on, practical experience in their field while contributing to real IBM projects. To be eligible, candidates must be currently enrolled at an accredited university and able to pause their coursework for the duration of the Co‑Op, as students may not be enrolled in classes while participating. This role requires full‑time availability (40 hours per week) during the Spring 2027 semester between Jan 19 - May 7. Eligible candidates should also be available to join IBM in a full‑time role between December 2027 and August 2028 upon successful completion of their degree.

We are looking for Software Developer Co-op students to join our engineering teams. As an intern, you will work alongside experienced IBM developers to design, build, and test software that powers our cloud, AI, and hybrid‑platform solutions. This role is designed for students who are passionate about coding—regardless of which programming language they started with. You will gain hands-on experience in real-world projects, learn modern development practices, and collaborate in an Agile environment where your ideas can make an immediate impact.

What You’ll Do

 Support the design, development, testing, and debugging of software in front-end, back-end, or full‑stack environments. Work with a variety of programming languages depending on the project (examples: Python, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, C++, Go, Rust, Swift, Kotlin, or others). Help build user interfaces using frameworks like React or contribute to back-end services and APIs. Use Git and other version‑control and collaboration tools. Work with cloud and container technologies such as Docker, Kubernetes, and REST APIs. Participate in Agile ceremonies, code reviews, and technical discussions. Explore emerging technologies, including AI/ML, automation, and cloud-native development.

Location Flexibility: By applying to this requisition, you acknowledge and agree to be considered for any of the listed locations associated with this position and are willing to work at the location where you are ultimately assigned.

Preferred Education

Bachelor's Degree

Required Technical And Professional Expertise

 Must be actively enrolled in a Bachelor’s degree program at the time of application and returning to complete the degree after the co-op. Available to start full-time between December 2027 and August 2028. Available to work full-time (40 hours/week) at an IBM location for 16 weeks between Jan 19 - May 7. Co-op requires a full-time commitment; students should not be enrolled in concurrent coursework during the co-op term.

(Guidelines — transferable skills are encouraged)

 Coursework or project experience in software development using any programming language. Familiarity with fundamental concepts such as data structures, basic algorithms, or debugging. Exposure to front-end or back-end technologies (React, Node.js, Python, Java, SQL, etc.). Experience using Git or similar version control tools. Interest in cloud computing, containers, or modern deployment practices. Strong analytical thinking, problem‑solving, and communication skills. Ability to collaborate and learn quickly in a team environment.

Preferred Technical And Professional Experience

 Experience with cloud services (IBM Cloud, AWS, Azure, or GCP). Familiarity with REST APIs and databases (relational or NoSQL). Exposure to CI/CD pipelines or automation tools. Personal or open-source projects that demonstrate creativity and initiative. Understanding of Agile development methods.

Machine Learning Engineer

About Proxima

Proxima (formerly VantAI) is advancing an AI-native approach to drug discovery by making protein interactions programmable. Our platform brings together foundation-model machine learning, a scalable data generation engine, and a partnership track record exceeding $5B in collaborations across the world’s leading biopharma and tech organizations. We’ve recently closed an oversubscribed seed round partnering us with an elite group of sophisticated and dedicated VCs including DCVC, Nvidia’s Nventures, AIX, and Yosemite among others.

Neo-1 is our all-atom foundation model that combines state-of-the-art structure prediction and molecular generation in a single system. Neo-1 enables rapid exploration of chemical and structural space for high-value, previously intractable targets, and in particular unlocks small molecule proximity therapeutics like molecular glues with AI for the first time.

In parallel, we are developing an advanced structural interactomics platform (NeoLink) built on proprietary XLMS technology and a lab equipped with next-generation mass spectrometry instrumentation. This platform produces proteome-scale maps of protein interactions and helps identify small molecules that modulate proximity. Together with Neo-1, it creates an integrated system capable of co-folding protein complexes while generating candidate small molecules to influence those interactions. Proximity-based therapeutics represent one of the most promising frontiers in modern drug discovery with the potential to treat previously intractable diseases and target ‘undruggable’ proteins. Our technology combines proteome-scale structural data with state-of-the-art generative AI foundation models and, coupled with our talented team of scientists and engineers, we are uniquely well-positioned to discover and develop a new class of medicines. Come join us!

About You

We are looking for a versatile software engineer to build the tools and systems behind our drug discovery research. You will work across automation, infrastructure, data, and ML, helping scientists develop models, run experiments, and use the results.

You enjoy taking a problem from investigation through deployment. Your work might involve integrating a dataset into training, diagnosing a stalled inference job, building an API for scientific results, or automating a manual workflow. You can find your way around an unfamiliar codebase, understand the constraints, and deliver a focused, well-tested improvement.

Our environment centers on Python and PyTorch, with containerized workloads, Kubernetes, cloud storage, and shared GPU compute. You will work closely with researchers and infrastructure engineers.

Relevant areas of expertise might include high-performance cloud computing, systems engineering, and machine learning, but specific knowledge of any of these areas is less critical than versatility and a willingness to learn and work anywhere in the tech stack. We value individuals who want to make an impact, have a deep intellectual curiosity, enjoy solving challenging problems, and have a track record of achievement.

Outcomes For This Role

Build reliable scientific workflows that colleagues can run, reproduce, and troubleshoot with less manual intervention.Integrate new models, datasets, and evaluation methods while preserving data correctness and compatibility with existing experiments.Improve compute workflows through better job submission, monitoring, failure recovery, and artifact tracking.Identify and remove bottlenecks in data preparation, execution, and evaluation so researchers can iterate faster.Deliver libraries, services, and developer tools that are easy to use and maintain, with appropriate tests, documentation, and monitoring.Contributing to the culture of a rapidly growing companyBeing challenged by your colleagues and learning something new every day

Specific Skills And Qualifications

Strong Python and software engineering fundamentals, including data structures, interface design, testing, concurrency, and systematic debugging.A track record of delivering software that other people use and depend on, including maintaining and troubleshooting it after release.Experience building or supporting ML or scientific computing workflows, with an understanding of how data, model execution, and evaluation fit together. PyTorch experience is a must.Experience running software on Linux, working with containers, and shipping changes through automated tests and CI/CD.Ability to break down ambiguous problems, make progress independently, and explain technical tradeoffs with evidence.Willingness to work across automation, infrastructure, data, and ML, with a strong sense of ownership and clear communication with scientists and engineers.Ability to use AI development tools effectively and take responsibility for the correctness and maintainability of the resulting code.

Experience with Kubernetes, cloud platforms, workflow orchestration, databases, or computational biology and chemistry is valuable. We welcome strong engineers from other technical domains; a biology or chemistry background is not required.

About The Opportunity

JOB SUMMARY

The Defense Industrial Base Institute at Northeastern University (NU) – a rapidly growing defense focused institute that conducts cutting-edge applied R&D – is seeking an experienced and highly capable Jr. Data Scientist with expertise in applying methods/frameworks/systems that apply ML&AI. The Jr. Data Scientist will operate as part of a multi-disciplinary team (academia, industry and government) and will contribute directly to the successful execution of federally funded projects/activities,

Responsibilities include providing technical expertise and analytical support to Principal investigators or co-principal investigators as a Jr. Data Scientist for a wide range of projects and activities involving machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI), including autonomy, sensing and communication, and decision support systems, among others. The Jr, Data Scientist will work collaboratively with and help guide, multi-disciplinary teams across the DIBI Higher Education Consortium — spanning academic, government, and industry partners — to design, validate, and maintain datasets and analytical products that inform institute leadership and sponsor decision-making. Specifically, the Jr. Data Scientist will take a role in building and maintaining the data pipelines and analytical components underlying the existing Navigator methodology, working closely with — and providing guidance to — data researchers, engineers, and leadership across the institute.

Successful candidates will be responsible team players and passionate about machine learning technologies, as well as possess a deep understanding of machine learning technology and experience in turning machine learning systems into practical, state-of-the-art systems that can be enhanced for projects or activities as per federal agency. About The Opportunity

Job Summary

Northeastern University seeks a Postdoctoral Research Associate to join a fixed-term, mixed-methods research initiative investigating the validity the International Big Picture Learning Credential (IBPLC) as a rigorous, equitable pathway into college admissions. The project — a partnership between Northeastern, Big Picture Learning U.S. (BPL U.S.), Big Picture Learning Australia (BPL Australia), and the National Association for College Admission Counseling (NACAC), and supported by the YTL Fund — examines whether the IBPLC predicts postsecondary success, whether advisors apply its assessment frames reliably and consistently, whether the credential measures what it claims to measure, and how admissions professionals come to trust it. The Postdoctoral Associate will work closely with the Principal Investigator(s) and partner organizations, with substantial input across all components of the study.

Responsibilities

Design and manage the longitudinal tracking system for enrolled IBPLC students, coordinating consent, data collection, and case-study protocols with BPL U.S. sitesConduct quantitative analysis of predictive validity, linking IBPLC scores and assessment data to first- and second-year college outcomes (grades, persistence, survey measures)Coordinate the reliability study: design observation protocols for IBPLC authorization training and school-based advisory case studies, and analyze consistency of advisor scoring across sitesSupport the construct validity aim by coordinating the subject matter expert panel reviewing IBPLC assessment frames across all six Learning Goals, and by analyzing alignment between frames and student performance dataDesign, field, and analyze annual admissions-leader focus groups, pilot application readings, and advisor and student surveys; lead qualitative coding of interview and focus group dataMaintain IRB protocols, data use agreements, and study documentationLead drafting of annual research summaries, the final comprehensive report, and dissemination products, including peer-reviewed manuscripts, practitioner-facing briefs, and conference presentationsAssist in administrative tasks of the study


Qualifications

Required:

PhD or EdD in education, educational measurement/psychometrics, sociology, higher education, or a related field, completed by the start dateDemonstrated mixed-methods research skills, including experience with longitudinal, predictive validity, or reliability designs and proficiency in R, SPSS, or comparable statistical softwareExperience with qualitative data collection and coding (e.g., interviews, focus groups, case studies) and familiarity with tools such as NVivo, Dedoose, or Atlas.tiExperience with survey design and administration (Qualtrics or equivalent) and rigorous data management practicesRecord of scholarly writing and demonstrated ability to communicate findings to practitioner and policy audiences


Preferred

Background in competency-based education, alternative credentials, or college admissions researchExperience with quantitative and psychometric analysesFamiliarity with National Student Clearinghouse data or other national postsecondary outcome datasetsExperience facilitating focus groups or expert panels with professional stakeholdersExperience managing multi-site IRB protocols and data use agreementsExperience in US high schools

rows.title: ML Engineer
rows.descriptionText:
Machine Learning Engineer

About Proxima

Proxima (formerly VantAI) is advancing an AI-native approach to drug discovery by making protein interactions programmable. Our platform brings together foundation-model machine learning, a scalable data generation engine, and a partnership track record exceeding $5B in collaborations across the world’s leading biopharma and tech organizations. We’ve recently closed an oversubscribed seed round partnering us with an elite group of sophisticated and dedicated VCs including DCVC, Nvidia’s Nventures, AIX, and Yosemite among others.

Neo-1 is our all-atom foundation model that combines state-of-the-art structure prediction and molecular generation in a single system. Neo-1 enables rapid exploration of chemical and structural space for high-value, previously intractable targets, and in particular unlocks small molecule proximity therapeutics like molecular glues with AI for the first time.

In parallel, we are developing an advanced structural interactomics platform (NeoLink) built on proprietary XLMS technology and a lab equipped with next-generation mass spectrometry instrumentation. This platform produces proteome-scale maps of protein interactions and helps identify small molecules that modulate proximity. Together with Neo-1, it creates an integrated system capable of co-folding protein complexes while generating candidate small molecules to influence those interactions. Proximity-based therapeutics represent one of the most promising frontiers in modern drug discovery with the potential to treat previously intractable diseases and target ‘undruggable’ proteins. Our technology combines proteome-scale structural data with state-of-the-art generative AI foundation models and, coupled with our talented team of scientists and engineers, we are uniquely well-positioned to discover and develop a new class of medicines. Come join us!

About You

We are looking for a versatile software engineer to build the tools and systems behind our drug discovery research. You will work across automation, infrastructure, data, and ML, helping scientists develop models, run experiments, and use the results.

You enjoy taking a problem from investigation through deployment. Your work might involve integrating a dataset into training, diagnosing a stalled inference job, building an API for scientific results, or automating a manual workflow. You can find your way around an unfamiliar codebase, understand the constraints, and deliver a focused, well-tested improvement.

Our environment centers on Python and PyTorch, with containerized workloads, Kubernetes, cloud storage, and shared GPU compute. You will work closely with researchers and infrastructure engineers.

Relevant areas of expertise might include high-performance cloud computing, systems engineering, and machine learning, but specific knowledge of any of these areas is less critical than versatility and a willingness to learn and work anywhere in the tech stack. We value individuals who want to make an impact, have a deep intellectual curiosity, enjoy solving challenging problems, and have a track record of achievement.

Outcomes For This Role

Build reliable scientific workflows that colleagues can run, reproduce, and troubleshoot with less manual intervention.Integrate new models, datasets, and evaluation methods while preserving data correctness and compatibility with existing experiments.Improve compute workflows through better job submission, monitoring, failure recovery, and artifact tracking.Identify and remove bottlenecks in data preparation, execution, and evaluation so researchers can iterate faster.Deliver libraries, services, and developer tools that are easy to use and maintain, with appropriate tests, documentation, and monitoring.Contributing to the culture of a rapidly growing companyBeing challenged by your colleagues and learning something new every day

Specific Skills And Qualifications

Strong Python and software engineering fundamentals, including data structures, interface design, testing, concurrency, and systematic debugging.A track record of delivering software that other people use and depend on, including maintaining and troubleshooting it after release.Experience building or supporting ML or scientific computing workflows, with an understanding of how data, model execution, and evaluation fit together. PyTorch experience is a must.Experience running software on Linux, working with containers, and shipping changes through automated tests and CI/CD.Ability to break down ambiguous problems, make progress independently, and explain technical tradeoffs with evidence.Willingness to work across automation, infrastructure, data, and ML, with a strong sense of ownership and clear communication with scientists and engineers.Ability to use AI development tools effectively and take responsibility for the correctness and maintainability of the resulting code.

Experience with Kubernetes, cloud platforms, workflow orchestration, databases, or computational biology and chemistry is valuable. We welcome strong engineers from other technical domains; a biology or chemistry background is not required.

rows.descriptionText:
About The Opportunity

Job Summary

Northeastern University seeks a Postdoctoral Research Associate to join a fixed-term, mixed-methods research initiative investigating the validity the International Big Picture Learning Credential (IBPLC) as a rigorous, equitable pathway into college admissions. The project — a partnership between Northeastern, Big Picture Learning U.S. (BPL U.S.), Big Picture Learning Australia (BPL Australia), and the National Association for College Admission Counseling (NACAC), and supported by the YTL Fund — examines whether the IBPLC predicts postsecondary success, whether advisors apply its assessment frames reliably and consistently, whether the credential measures what it claims to measure, and how admissions professionals come to trust it. The Postdoctoral Associate will work closely with the Principal Investigator(s) and partner organizations, with substantial input across all components of the study.

Responsibilities

Design and manage the longitudinal tracking system for enrolled IBPLC students, coordinating consent, data collection, and case-study protocols with BPL U.S. sitesConduct quantitative analysis of predictive validity, linking IBPLC scores and assessment data to first- and second-year college outcomes (grades, persistence, survey measures)Coordinate the reliability study: design observation protocols for IBPLC authorization training and school-based advisory case studies, and analyze consistency of advisor scoring across sitesSupport the construct validity aim by coordinating the subject matter expert panel reviewing IBPLC assessment frames across all six Learning Goals, and by analyzing alignment between frames and student performance dataDesign, field, and analyze annual admissions-leader focus groups, pilot application readings, and advisor and student surveys; lead qualitative coding of interview and focus group dataMaintain IRB protocols, data use agreements, and study documentationLead drafting of annual research summaries, the final comprehensive report, and dissemination products, including peer-reviewed manuscripts, practitioner-facing briefs, and conference presentationsAssist in administrative tasks of the study


Qualifications

Required:

PhD or EdD in education, educational measurement/psychometrics, sociology, higher education, or a related field, completed by the start dateDemonstrated mixed-methods research skills, including experience with longitudinal, predictive validity, or reliability designs and proficiency in R, SPSS, or comparable statistical softwareExperience with qualitative data collection and coding (e.g., interviews, focus groups, case studies) and familiarity with tools such as NVivo, Dedoose, or Atlas.tiExperience with survey design and administration (Qualtrics or equivalent) and rigorous data management practicesRecord of scholarly writing and demonstrated ability to communicate findings to practitioner and policy audiences


Preferred

Background in competency-based education, alternative credentials, or college admissions researchExperience with quantitative and psychometric analysesFamiliarity with National Student Clearinghouse data or other national postsecondary outcome datasetsExperience facilitating focus groups or expert panels with professional stakeholdersExperience managing multi-site IRB protocols and data use agreementsExperience in US high schools


Position Details

Grant-funded appointment, contingent on funding and satisfactory performance and renewable based on available fundingSalary commensurate with experience, consistent with Northeastern postdoctoral scales, plus standard benefitsBoston campus, hybrid schedule; some domestic travel expectedReports to the Principal Investigator(s) of the IBPLC Validity & Implementation StudyApplications without a Cover Letter will not be considered

rows.title: ML Engineer
rows.descriptionText:
Machine Learning Engineer

About Proxima

Proxima (formerly VantAI) is advancing an AI-native approach to drug discovery by making protein interactions programmable. Our platform brings together foundation-model machine learning, a scalable data generation engine, and a partnership track record exceeding $5B in collaborations across the world’s leading biopharma and tech organizations. We’ve recently closed an oversubscribed seed round partnering us with an elite group of sophisticated and dedicated VCs including DCVC, Nvidia’s Nventures, AIX, and Yosemite among others.

Neo-1 is our all-atom foundation model that combines state-of-the-art structure prediction and molecular generation in a single system. Neo-1 enables rapid exploration of chemical and structural space for high-value, previously intractable targets, and in particular unlocks small molecule proximity therapeutics like molecular glues with AI for the first time.

In parallel, we are developing an advanced structural interactomics platform (NeoLink) built on proprietary XLMS technology and a lab equipped with next-generation mass spectrometry instrumentation. This platform produces proteome-scale maps of protein interactions and helps identify small molecules that modulate proximity. Together with Neo-1, it creates an integrated system capable of co-folding protein complexes while generating candidate small molecules to influence those interactions. Proximity-based therapeutics represent one of the most promising frontiers in modern drug discovery with the potential to treat previously intractable diseases and target ‘undruggable’ proteins. Our technology combines proteome-scale structural data with state-of-the-art generative AI foundation models and, coupled with our talented team of scientists and engineers, we are uniquely well-positioned to discover and develop a new class of medicines. Come join us!

About You

We are looking for a versatile software engineer to build the tools and systems behind our drug discovery research. You will work across automation, infrastructure, data, and ML, helping scientists develop models, run experiments, and use the results.

You enjoy taking a problem from investigation through deployment. Your work might involve integrating a dataset into training, diagnosing a stalled inference job, building an API for scientific results, or automating a manual workflow. You can find your way around an unfamiliar codebase, understand the constraints, and deliver a focused, well-tested improvement.

Our environment centers on Python and PyTorch, with containerized workloads, Kubernetes, cloud storage, and shared GPU compute. You will work closely with researchers and infrastructure engineers.

Relevant areas of expertise might include high-performance cloud computing, systems engineering, and machine learning, but specific knowledge of any of these areas is less critical than versatility and a willingness to learn and work anywhere in the tech stack. We value individuals who want to make an impact, have a deep intellectual curiosity, enjoy solving challenging problems, and have a track record of achievement.

Outcomes For This Role

Build reliable scientific workflows that colleagues can run, reproduce, and troubleshoot with less manual intervention.Integrate new models, datasets, and evaluation methods while preserving data correctness and compatibility with existing experiments.Improve compute workflows through better job submission, monitoring, failure recovery, and artifact tracking.Identify and remove bottlenecks in data preparation, execution, and evaluation so researchers can iterate faster.Deliver libraries, services, and developer tools that are easy to use and maintain, with appropriate tests, documentation, and monitoring.Contributing to the culture of a rapidly growing companyBeing challenged by your colleagues and learning something new every day

Specific Skills And Qualifications

Strong Python and software engineering fundamentals, including data structures, interface design, testing, concurrency, and systematic debugging.A track record of delivering software that other people use and depend on, including maintaining and troubleshooting it after release.Experience building or supporting ML or scientific computing workflows, with an understanding of how data, model execution, and evaluation fit together. PyTorch experience is a must.Experience running software on Linux, working with containers, and shipping changes through automated tests and CI/CD.Ability to break down ambiguous problems, make progress independently, and explain technical tradeoffs with evidence.Willingness to work across automation, infrastructure, data, and ML, with a strong sense of ownership and clear communication with scientists and engineers.Ability to use AI development tools effectively and take responsibility for the correctness and maintainability of the resulting code.

Experience with Kubernetes, cloud platforms, workflow orchestration, databases, or computational biology and chemistry is valuable. We welcome strong engineers from other technical domains; a biology or chemistry background is not required.

As a member of the Airborne Radar Systems and Techniques group at MIT Lincoln Laboratory, you will work on high-performance sensor systems as part of a team with varied technical backgrounds. We prototype radar and imaging sensors for wide-area surveillance, and work to mature algorithms to detect small objects in challenging environments. Projects typically involve a mix of hardware and software development, as well as algorithm design. Teams work together to understand foundational physical principles, design and build one-of-a-kind sensor systems, architect and execute flight test data collections, develop and integrate novel processing techniques, and explore advanced countermeasures that degrade sensor performance. Staff projects typically partner across the Department of Defense to transition work onto platforms that operate around the globe, and perform impactful and relevant missions.

Position Description

MIT Lincoln Laboratory is seeking a talented researcher to join our dynamic team as a radar systems analyst with a focus in signal processing and data analysis. As a member of the Airborne Radar Systems and Techniques group at MIT Lincoln Laboratory, you will work on world-class sensor systems as part of a team with a variety of technical backgrounds. We model and analyze the performance of new technologies, prototype radio frequency and complimentary sensors, design and execute data collections, and develop algorithms to detect, track, and image challenging targets within complex environments. Our models and algorithms benefit from access to a one-of-a-kind interactive supercomputer. Our prototypes and data collections are enabled by highly adaptable test infrastructure including two airborne radar testbeds—turboprop aircraft equipped with an advanced radars, visible and infrared imaging system, communications systems, and real-time data processors and modern jammers.

We are particularly interested in candidates with a PhD (or MS with 5-10 years of relevant experience) in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, or a related field who work well within a team environment. Our work involves a mix of new concept and algorithm development, radar and electronic warfare systems modeling, experiment design, and data-driven analysis. As such, we expect candidates to have significant experience in digital signal processing or expertise in the underlying mathematics and computational techniques and interest in applying those skills to active and passive sensing systems, RF communications, and electronic warfare systems.

rows.title: ML Engineer
rows.descriptionText:
Machine Learning Engineer

About Proxima

Proxima (formerly VantAI) is advancing an AI-native approach to drug discovery by making protein interactions programmable. Our platform brings together foundation-model machine learning, a scalable data generation engine, and a partnership track record exceeding $5B in collaborations across the world’s leading biopharma and tech organizations. We’ve recently closed an oversubscribed seed round partnering us with an elite group of sophisticated and dedicated VCs including DCVC, Nvidia’s Nventures, AIX, and Yosemite among others.

Neo-1 is our all-atom foundation model that combines state-of-the-art structure prediction and molecular generation in a single system. Neo-1 enables rapid exploration of chemical and structural space for high-value, previously intractable targets, and in particular unlocks small molecule proximity therapeutics like molecular glues with AI for the first time.

In parallel, we are developing an advanced structural interactomics platform (NeoLink) built on proprietary XLMS technology and a lab equipped with next-generation mass spectrometry instrumentation. This platform produces proteome-scale maps of protein interactions and helps identify small molecules that modulate proximity. Together with Neo-1, it creates an integrated system capable of co-folding protein complexes while generating candidate small molecules to influence those interactions. Proximity-based therapeutics represent one of the most promising frontiers in modern drug discovery with the potential to treat previously intractable diseases and target ‘undruggable’ proteins. Our technology combines proteome-scale structural data with state-of-the-art generative AI foundation models and, coupled with our talented team of scientists and engineers, we are uniquely well-positioned to discover and develop a new class of medicines. Come join us!

About You

We are looking for a versatile software engineer to build the tools and systems behind our drug discovery research. You will work across automation, infrastructure, data, and ML, helping scientists develop models, run experiments, and use the results.

You enjoy taking a problem from investigation through deployment. Your work might involve integrating a dataset into training, diagnosing a stalled inference job, building an API for scientific results, or automating a manual workflow. You can find your way around an unfamiliar codebase, understand the constraints, and deliver a focused, well-tested improvement.

Our environment centers on Python and PyTorch, with containerized workloads, Kubernetes, cloud storage, and shared GPU compute. You will work closely with researchers and infrastructure engineers.

Relevant areas of expertise might include high-performance cloud computing, systems engineering, and machine learning, but specific knowledge of any of these areas is less critical than versatility and a willingness to learn and work anywhere in the tech stack. We value individuals who want to make an impact, have a deep intellectual curiosity, enjoy solving challenging problems, and have a track record of achievement.

Outcomes For This Role

Build reliable scientific workflows that colleagues can run, reproduce, and troubleshoot with less manual intervention.Integrate new models, datasets, and evaluation methods while preserving data correctness and compatibility with existing experiments.Improve compute workflows through better job submission, monitoring, failure recovery, and artifact tracking.Identify and remove bottlenecks in data preparation, execution, and evaluation so researchers can iterate faster.Deliver libraries, services, and developer tools that are easy to use and maintain, with appropriate tests, documentation, and monitoring.Contributing to the culture of a rapidly growing companyBeing challenged by your colleagues and learning something new every day

Specific Skills And Qualifications

Strong Python and software engineering fundamentals, including data structures, interface design, testing, concurrency, and systematic debugging.A track record of delivering software that other people use and depend on, including maintaining and troubleshooting it after release.Experience building or supporting ML or scientific computing workflows, with an understanding of how data, model execution, and evaluation fit together. PyTorch experience is a must.Experience running software on Linux, working with containers, and shipping changes through automated tests and CI/CD.Ability to break down ambiguous problems, make progress independently, and explain technical tradeoffs with evidence.Willingness to work across automation, infrastructure, data, and ML, with a strong sense of ownership and clear communication with scientists and engineers.Ability to use AI development tools effectively and take responsibility for the correctness and maintainability of the resulting code.

Experience with Kubernetes, cloud platforms, workflow orchestration, databases, or computational biology and chemistry is valuable. We welcome strong engineers from other technical domains; a biology or chemistry background is not required.
